title: Constrain AnalyticsService.logEvent to the AnalyticsEvent catalog — LogEvents-sourced calls leak profile_id and content identifiers to Firebase Analytics

evidence.quote: // Typed string constants for structured log event names.

why: AnalyticsService.logEvent(String name, ...) accepts any bare string, so nothing stops a caller from importing LogEvents — documented in its own header as 'structured log event names' for AppLogger, not an analytics catalog — and piping it straight into real Firebase Analytics. Grepping every `.logEvent(` call site in lib/ shows ~15 places do exactly this, bypassing the audited 12-event AnalyticsEvent catalog and its PV-1 review entirely. At least 7 of those sites attach identifying data: outbox_processor.dart fires sync_outbox_dead_lettered with entity_key = '${profileId}:${sefariaRef}:${stageId}:${trackType}:${curriculumId}' (confirmed composition in completion_writer.dart:747) for every dead-lettered completion row — combining the per-child profile id with the exact Torah/Mishnah reference the child was studying in one string; pull_pipeline.dart fires sync_merge_router_halt with a bare profile_id; tutor_pin_service.dart fires tutor_pin_set with a bare profile_id; tutor_audit_log_writer.dart fires tutor_action_recorded with a 'target' field whose own documented shape is a resource path like 'profile/42.displayName' (line 130) — i.e. the profile id again, now attached to a description of what was changed; sync_orchestrator.dart fires sync_pull_failed and sync_listener_error with the raw exception's `.toString()`, which for Firestore permission/not-found errors routinely embeds the full document resource path (profiles/{id}/completions/{ref}). In release/profile builds analyticsServiceProvider resolves to the real FirebaseAnalyticsService (analytics_provider.dart), whose logEvent forwards `parameters` verbatim with zero redaction (firebase_analytics_service.dart:29-32) — so every one of these fires a real event to Google's servers. This is materially worse than the two baselined single-field leaks (bare sefaria_ref, bare profile_id in analytics_service.dart) because several of these sites combine per-child identity with content/action detail in one uncatalogued, unreviewed string, and remains a live COPPA/GDPR-K risk independent of the separately-baselined PV-3 consent-gating gap (fixing consent gating controls whether these fire at all, not what's inside them once a user has consented).
recommendation: Change AnalyticsService.logEvent's name parameter from bare String to a closed type sourced only from AnalyticsEvent (e.g. an extension type/sealed wrapper), add a Rule-0 grep/lint that fails CI on any `.logEvent(` call whose first argument isn't `AnalyticsEvent.<x>`, and triage the 7 cited sites: either drop the identifying parameter and keep these as AppLogger-only structured logs (most already have a parallel LogEvents-based AppLogger call right next to the analytics one), or promote them into AnalyticsEvent with PV-1-safe parameters (counts/enums/booleans only) and route error detail through a stable EH-5 error-code enum instead of `.toString()`.
acceptance_criteria: A checker (grep in make audit, or a working custom_lint rule) fails with file:line on any AnalyticsService.logEvent(...)/.logEvent( call whose event-name argument is not an AnalyticsEvent member
entity_key/profile_id/target/error-text parameters are removed, hashed, or replaced with a coarse enum at all 7 cited call sites

A regression test asserts FakeAnalyticsService-captured params for outbox_dead_lettered, merge_router_halt, pull_failed, listener_error, tutor_pin_set, and tutor_action_recorded never contain a raw profileId, sefariaRef, or exception string
docs/coding-standards.md PV-1 known-gaps list is either cleared for these sites or explicitly extended to name them

The finding's 'sites: 7' should read 6 confirmed-reachable + 1 dormant; this does not change the verdict or severity since 6 live production leak sites remain independently confirmed, including one (entity_key) that combines profile_id with content identifier in a single string.

title: Add profileId FK+CASCADE to 6 tables — tutored-mirror wipe currently orphans a mirrored child's data
rule: profileId-in-PK Invariant / DB-6 (sync-able entity integrity, FK-cascade discipline)

evidence.quote: the learner_profiles row cascades to all mirrored rows in completions, ... curriculum_tracks, etc. No explicit child-row deletion is needed.
The FK `ON DELETE CASCADE` on every child table (completions, streak_events, learning_ledger, bookmarks, goals, etc.)
// `outbox` has no FK — without this its pending pushes for the deleted profile would survive.

why: None of these 6 tables declare `.references(LearnerProfiles, #id, onDelete: KeyAction.cascade)` on their profileId column (every sibling table that IS correctly protected does). `ProfileRepositoryImpl.deleteProfile()` compensates by explicitly deleting from all 6 before removing the profile row — the team clearly knows about this gap. But `TutoredMirrorWipeService.wipeMirrorForGrant/wipeAllMirrors/wipeRevokedMirrors` (used on tutor grant revoke/resign, tutor sign-out, and the D18 revoke-reconcile path) does NOT replicate that compensation — it only calls `ProfileDao.deleteTutoredMirrorByGrantId`, a bare delete of the `learner_profiles` row, while its own top-of-file comment incorrectly asserts universal FK cascade covering `curriculum_tracks, etc.`. `tutored_pull_service.dart` (line 99, 'a point_configs FK violation') confirms these tables are actually populated for a live mirror. Net effect: when a tutoring relationship ends, the tutored child's mirrored curriculum_tracks/daily_plans/point_configs/profile_programs/study_day_configs rows silently persist on the tutor's device forever — a child-privacy data-retention failure that contradicts the code's own stated invariant, with no error or log to reveal it.
recommendation: Either (a) add `.references(LearnerProfiles, #id, onDelete: KeyAction.cascade)` to profileId on all 6 tables (schema migration + schema export per DB-4), or (b) make `TutoredMirrorWipeService` explicitly delete from all 6 tables before removing the `learner_profiles` row, mirroring `ProfileRepositoryImpl.deleteProfile`'s existing pattern (no migration needed, lower risk, matches established precedent). Fix the false comment either way.
acceptance_criteria: New regression test: after wipeMirrorForGrant/wipeAllMirrors, querying curriculum_tracks/daily_plans/outbox/point_configs/profile_programs/study_day_configs WHERE profileId = <wiped id> returns 0 rows.
tutored_mirror_wipe_service.dart's header comment no longer claims universal FK cascade for tables that don't have it.

tool/schema_check.dart (or a new companion checker) flags any core/database/tables profileId column lacking a `.references(LearnerProfiles, ...)` FK, so a future new table can't silently reintroduce the gap.

corrections: The "rule" field's mapping is imprecise: I searched coding-standards.md in full and neither DB-6 nor the profileId-in-PK Invariant actually mentions FK cascade/onDelete behavior anywhere (grep for "cascade|onDelete|foreign key" in the doc returns zero hits) — DB-6 is about local-first write/watch/reconcile, and profileId-in-PK is about composite-PK column presence, not delete-cascade semantics. The underlying defect is real and well-evidenced (verified by direct code reading, not just quotes), but it isn't actually a violation of the two named rules' literal text — it's closer to an unstated data-integrity/child-privacy principle. Also worth flagging for the fix-author: outbox's inclusion in the "6 tables" is less certain — code comments suggest tutored-profile pushes are drain-guarded (never sent), so it's not fully confirmed outbox rows are ever created for a tutored mirror in the first place, though this doesn't undermine the other 5 tables.

Rule citation is imprecise: "profileId-in-PK Invariant" (composite-PK requirement) and DB-6 (local-first sync pattern) don't literally mandate FK-cascade; no coding-standards.md rule is explicitly titled "FK-cascade discipline" — closest textual anchor is the Privacy & Child Data section's general concern about orphaned privacy-sensitive child data. Also, the profile_repository_impl.dart:232 quote actually starts at line 230 ("...FK-cascade ordering. `outbox` has no FK — without this") and continues to 231, a 2-line citation offset. Neither issue undermines the underlying defect, which is real and well-evidenced.

title: Stop ProfileRepositoryImpl.updateProfile silently swallowing tutor Cloud-Function write failures
rule: EH-2/EH-3 (typed errors must reach a boundary as values, no log-less catch) + Nygard lens (retry-assumption mismatch across facade implementations)

evidence.quote:
} catch (_) {
      // no-op: cloud push failure is non-fatal; local write already succeeded (offline-first)

/// When a tutor session is active ([activeTutoredProfileSelectionProvider] !=
/// null) the outbox facade is wrapped by a [TutoredWriteRouter]

} catch (_) {
      // no-op: cloud push failure is non-fatal; local write already succeeded (offline-first)

} catch (_) {
      // no-op: cloud push failure is non-fatal; local write already succeeded.

why: ProfileRepositoryImpl wraps every _syncEngine?.pushLearnerProfile(...) call in a blanket catch(_) {} (createProfile:104-109, updateProfile:157-161, self-heal:321-336), on the premise that 'local write already succeeded (offline-first)' and the push will retry later. That premise only holds when _syncEngine is the durable OutboxSyncWriteFacade. Per sync_providers.dart:75-78, when a tutor session is active, _syncEngine is instead a TutoredWriteRouter that turns pushLearnerProfile into a one-shot, non-retryable Cloud Function RPC (tutorEditProfile). When that RPC fails (network drop, CF timeout, or the tutor's grant expiring mid-session), the failure is discarded: updateProfile still returns its local model as if the push succeeded, so the tutor's own local mirror shows the rename/mode/avatar change permanently while the owner's actual Firestore profile was never touched — a silent, non-retryable divergence between what the tutor sees and what actually persisted, with zero error surfaced. This also makes editProfileFlow's dedicated 'on TutorWriteException catch' (profile_edit_delete_actions.dart:46) dead code: repo.updateProfile can only ever let StateError or DuplicateProfileNameException (line 134) escape to its caller, and editProfileFlow doesn't catch the latter at all, so even a same-account name collision on the Edit flow throws unhandled — unlike ProfilePickerScreen's own separate rename dialog, which does catch DuplicateProfileNameException. profile_edit_delete_actions_test.dart exercises neither path (zero references to TutorWriteException or DuplicateProfileNameException in the whole file).
recommendation: Only swallow pushLearnerProfile failures when the underlying facade is genuinely durable/retryable (OutboxSyncWriteFacade); let a TutorWriteException-shaped failure propagate (or convert it to a typed Result the caller must handle) so editProfileFlow's existing catch becomes reachable and can tell the tutor the edit didn't save. Add a catch for DuplicateProfileNameException in editProfileFlow mirroring profile_picker_screen.dart's _showRenameDialog.

title: Redact TransactionalEmail.plaintextBody before logging in LoggingTransactionalEmailService.send()
rule: Child-privacy logging hygiene (PV-family principle) — breaks the PiiRedactor.sensitiveKeys contract in core/logging/logger.dart that the same function's sibling field already relies on

evidence.quote: '$tutorEmail has declined your invitation to tutor $childName.\n\n'

why: LoggingTransactionalEmailService.send() (the only bound TransactionalEmailService implementation today) logs the full plaintextBody under the key 'body' via AppLogger.instance.debug(). PiiRedactor.redactFields() only blanks values whose KEY is in the 49-entry sensitiveKeys allowlist (logger.dart:203-251) — 'body' is not in it, even though 'to'/'recipient'/'email_to' were deliberately added and regression-tested (test/core/logging/logger_extended_test.dart:271-304, tag V2-R5 C2) for the exact same call site two lines above. title: Verify emailVerified (or the invite_token) before granting tutor-invite acceptance by email match

evidence.quote: // This prevents anyone from claiming an invite not addressed to them.
// without needing the emailed deep link. Match the caller's verified email.

why: Firebase Auth lets anyone register an account with any unverified email string. acceptTutorInvite, declineTutorInvite, and listTutorGrants({mode:'pending_for_me'}) all authorize 'is this caller the invited tutor' purely by comparing the caller's Auth email to grant.tutor_email -- none of them checks callerRecord.emailVerified (or the token claim), despite comments at both call sites explicitly (and incorrectly) claiming this 'prevents anyone from claiming an invite not addressed to them' / matches the 'verified' email. An attacker who front-runs registration of the invited tutor's email address can call listTutorGrants(pending_for_me) to discover the grantId, then acceptTutorInvite to gain ongoing read access (and any write permissions the parent granted) to the child's full learning profile -- without ever proving ownership of that inbox. The invite_token generated specifically to prevent exactly this (comment: 'single-use, per NFR-3') is stored on the grant doc but is never read back or compared anywhere in the file, so it provides zero actual protection. cf_grant_invite.test.mjs's own header comment confirms this exact gate is never exercised by any test.
recommendation: Require callerRecord.emailVerified === true in acceptTutorInvite/declineTutorInvite before trusting the email match, and/or require the caller to supply invite_token and compare it against grant.invite_token (the mechanism already built for this). Apply the same emailVerified gate to listTutorGrants' pending_for_me query so an unverified account cannot even discover invites addressed to an email it doesn't own.
acceptance_criteria: A new Auth-emulator-backed test in cf_grant_invite.test.mjs seeds an unverified-email account and asserts acceptTutorInvite rejects it (e.g. permission-denied).
acceptTutorInvite/declineTutorInvite check emailVerified or invite_token before authorizing by email match.
make test-functions (or a new CI job per the companion finding) seeds Auth-emulator users so this path is actually exercised, not skipped.

The doc has no explicit rule for CF invite-acceptance identity verification, so this is a thematic/nearest-analog citation rather than a verbatim match. Does not weaken the underlying defect, which is real and severe.

title: Fix missing synthetic-container guard in items_learned_providers.dart:computeLifetimeViewSummary (composite-curriculum over-credit regression)

title: account_lifecycle_service.dart removeCloudFromDevice() must verify the outbox is drained before deleting the local DB file

why: The outbox (tier-gated to cloud-born accounts, features/sync/presentation/providers/sync_providers.dart) queues Firestore writes locally until drained; those rows are the only copy of a mutation until push succeeds. removeCloudFromDevice() is reachable mid-session via swipe-to-dismiss in the Account Picker with zero connectivity check and zero OutboxDao.depth() check, then unconditionally deletes the account's entire local Drift file (which holds the outbox table) and the registry row. evidence.quote:

why: Every natural-key LWW merger applies the remote row (_store.upsert, which writes the entity table including its own updatedAt column) and THEN separately persists the SyncKv shadow timestamp (_store.persistUpdatedAt) as two independent awaited Drift writes with no enclosing db.transaction(). If the process dies between the two — an OS kill or force-quit on mobile is routine, not exotic — the entity row is left holding the remote's updatedAt while SyncKv still holds the pre-merge value. Any local edit made before the next successful sync now races a STALE local timestamp: a re-pulled, unchanged remote row will look newer than the stale SyncKv record and DriftMergeStore.remoteIsNewer will silently let it overwrite the user's genuinely-newer local edit — no exception, no log, nothing to retry against. This is DB-2's 'crash mid-sequence leaves the DB half-written' failure applied to the LWW bookkeeping itself.
recommendation: Add a MergeStore.applyRemote(...) that wraps the entity write and its SyncKv persistUpdatedAt in one db.transaction() (or expose a transaction-scoped variant), and switch all 8 callers to it.
acceptance_criteria: Fault-injection/unit test: call upsert() alone (simulating a crash before persistUpdatedAt commits), then perform a legitimately-newer local edit to the same row, then re-merge the identical stale remote row — assert the local edit survives.

corrections: 3 of the 8 sites (bookmark_merger.dart, goal_merger.dart, learning_order_merger.dart) have a redundant per-DAO LWW guard (e.g. BookmarkDao.upsertBookmarkByProfile checks `updatedAt.isAfter(existing.updatedAt)`) that partially mitigates the concrete overwrite outcome for those entities even though the transactional gap is real; the other 5 sites (trackConfig, learnerProfile, stageDefinition, profileProgram, settings) have no such backstop and are fully exposed to the described silent-overwrite failure. title: Give OutboxProcessor's single-flight guard a generation token so stale-reclaim can't run concurrent drains

evidence.quote: // reclaim only inspects the *same instance's* private state we also

why: The single-flight guard is two plain fields (_draining/_drainingSince) with no per-invocation identity. In production, OutboxProcessor is built with unmodified defaults (outbox_providers.dart:98-105: pushTimeout/drainStaleAfter never overridden) and sync_orchestrator.dart fires a periodic drain every 60s forever (Timer.periodic(_periodicDrainInterval, ...)) while drainStaleAfter is 90s. Non-completion kinds are pushed one row at a time, individually awaited (up to 50 rows x ~18 kinds) — a real multi-kind backlog on a slow connection easily exceeds 90s. When that happens, the next periodic (or connectivity/lifecycle) trigger sees the guard as 'stale', resets it, and starts a second, genuinely concurrent `_doDrain()` while the first is still running — the code comment at line 206-211 only reasons about two *reclaimers* racing each other synchronously; it never accounts for the *original* stale-but-still-running drain's own `finally` unconditionally zeroing `_draining`/`_drainingSince` once it eventually completes, which can then let a THIRD trigger barge in on top of the second. This directly breaks the documented contract ('collapses them to one push round' / sync_orchestrator.dart:568 'the OutboxProcessor's single-flight guard collapses races with other triggers'), producing duplicate concurrent Firestore pushes and racy interleaved deleteRow/markAttempted calls that can double-count a row's attempts and dead-letter a recoverable failure roughly twice as fast as _maxAttempts=10 implies. The R6-13 regression test that targets exactly this code path never builds true overlap: every scenario releases and awaits the 'wedged' pipeline to full completion before the next drain runs (its own comment admits the limitation at line 1392/1396), so the actual race is untested.
recommendation: Replace the boolean+timestamp guard with a construct that can tell 'my invocation' apart from a later reclaimer — e.g. a monotonically increasing generation counter captured at acquire time, checked before `finally` clears state (`if (_generation == myGeneration) { _draining = false; ... }`), or switch to chaining onto the in-flight Future (a late caller awaits/joins the existing drain rather than racing a flag).
acceptance_criteria: New/updated unit test keeps the first drain's pipeline call parked on a Completer, advances the clock past drainStaleAfter, drives a second (reclaiming) drain to full completion, then completes the first — and asserts the pipeline was invoked exactly once for the outstanding rows, or that DAO state is never corrupted by true overlap.
Guard implementation carries a generation token (or equivalent) so a finally block from an earlier invocation cannot clear state established by a later one.

corrections: The finding's characterization of the R6-13 test as "never builds true overlap" is only partially accurate. Two of its three sub-scenarios (p and p2) do complete the wedged drain before proceeding. But the third sub-scenario (p3, using _TogglePipeline, lines 1440-1483) genuinely does produce true overlap: setting `hang=false` does not unblock the already-parked first call (only affects future calls), so `reclaimedCount = await p3.drain(profileId)` at line 1464 runs concurrently with the still-suspended wedgedDrain3. However, the test asserts nothing about the consequence of that overlap (no pipeline-invocation-count or DAO-corruption assertion, just `>=1`), so the finding's substantive point — no regression test guards against duplicate/racy work from true overlap — still holds even though the "never builds true overlap" phrasing overstates the test's limitation.

title: Add UNIQUE(profileId, ulid) to PointsLedger and RewardRedemptions — sync merge can double-credit a child's points
rule: DB-6 (sync-able entity integrity) / profileId-in-PK's composite-index companion requirement
why: PointsLedger and RewardRedemptions both carry a `ulid` column documented as "cross-device id for append-only cloud sync" — the exact same purpose LearningLedger's `ulid` serves, where it is protected by a real `UNIQUE(profileId, ulid)` @TableIndex. Neither PointsLedger nor RewardRedemptions has any uniqueKeys/@TableIndex at all. PointsLedgerMerger's own comment says entries are "deduplicated on ulid via INSERT-OR-IGNORE," but points_balance_dao.dart's insertRemoteLedgerEntryIfAbsent actually does a manual SELECT-then-INSERT with no DB constraint backing it — a classic TOCTOU race. If two merge calls for the same ulid ever interleave (concurrent pulls, a retried tutored pull, a future refactor that parallelizes merges), a duplicate row lands; reDeriveBalanceFromLedger sums ALL ledger deltas, so the child's points balance silently becomes wrong — violating the table's own documented invariant that balance is "the authoritative denormalised sum of all ledger entries."
recommendation: Add `@TableIndex(name: 'points_ledger_profile_ulid', columns: {#profileId, #ulid}, unique: true)` to PointsLedger and an equivalent unique index to RewardRedemptions (mirroring learning_ledger.dart), ship as a schema migration, and switch insertRemoteLedgerEntryIfAbsent to rely on that constraint (insertOnConflictDoNothing) instead of a separate SELECT.
acceptance_criteria: Schema migration adds the unique index to points_ledger and reward_redemptions, with committed schema export + generated migration test (DB-4).
Regression test: calling the merge path twice concurrently (Future.wait) with the same ulid results in exactly one row and exactly one balance credit.

corrections: The "rule" field's sub-clause "profileId-in-PK's composite-index companion requirement" is the finding author's own paraphrase/inference, not verbatim text from DB-6 in coding-standards.md (DB-6 literally only mandates local-first write/watch/reconcile, not unique-index requirements). title: Resolve profileId live, not by snapshot, when wiring OutboxSyncWriteFacade/LocalDataUploadService/PointsBalanceDao.syncSink in syncOrchestratorProvider
rule: sync push/pull invariant (docs/sync-conflict-resolution.md) / Nygard-lens: stale capture
why: syncOrchestratorProvider is a keepAlive singleton that (by explicit design, per its own comments and resolveProfileIdProvider's doc) survives a profile switch without rebuilding, reacting only via `ref.listen(activeProfileIdProvider, ...)` to restart listeners. But `profileId` at line 79 is a one-time ref.read snapshot baked into OutboxSyncWriteFacade/LocalDataUploadService and into pointsBalanceDao.syncSink — not the lazy `resolveProfileId` the same function already builds at line 68 for the orchestrator's own calls. OutboxSyncWriteFacade._enqueue (features/sync/data/outbox_sync_write_facade.dart) stamps every outbox row's `profileId` column from this captured field for every entity kind it handles except learner-profile-delete (bookmarks, settings, goals, learning order, curriculum tracks, notification/gamification/UI-preference snapshots, streak events, study-day configs, and — via PointsBalanceDao._pushRedemption calling sink.enqueueRewardRedemption — reward redemptions). OutboxProcessor._doDrain only sweeps the currently-active profileId plus account-level 0 (confirmed in outbox_processor.dart and explicitly documented for the analogous deleteLearnerProfile case: 'the drain only sweeps the ACTIVE profile + 0... orphans the row'). So after a household profile switch (Bug #1/R1 already proves this happens mid-session without an orchestrator rebuild), every write of the affected kinds for the newly-active profile gets tagged with the stale boot-time profileId and is never drained until — if ever — that exact stale profile becomes active again. Concretely: parent app open with childA active, orchestrator built (profileId=A); parent switches to childB; childB redeems a reward or a bookmark/goal/track change is made; the outbox row is stamped profileId=A; the orchestrator's periodic/lifecycle/connectivity drains all resolve the live profileId (=B) and never pick up the A-stamped row. That data silently never reaches Firestore / other devices.
recommendation: Change OutboxSyncWriteFacade and LocalDataUploadService to take an `int Function() resolveProfileId` (reuse resolveProfileIdProvider) instead of a captured `int profileId`, reading it at each call instead of at construction. Re-wire pointsBalanceDao.syncSink and re-run reEnqueueUnsyncedLedgerRows whenever the active profile changes, not just once at orchestrator build.
acceptance_criteria: OutboxSyncWriteFacade/LocalDataUploadService read the active profile id live at write time rather than at construction time.

Regression test: build a ProviderContainer, go cloud-born with profile A active, switch activeProfileIdProvider to B, perform a write that reaches OutboxSyncWriteFacade, and assert the resulting outbox row's profileId column equals B, not A.

title: Wire onError (and a recovery-pull path) into TutoredListenerSupervisor's inner ListenerSupervisor

why: TutoredListenerSupervisor.attach() builds its ListenerSupervisor with only `source` and `onEvent` -- no `onError`, no `recoveryPullTriggers`. Inside ListenerSupervisor.start(), a stream error calls `_onError?.call(...)`, which is a silent no-op when `_onError` is null. Firestore terminates a `.snapshots()` stream on error (e.g. permission-denied when a parent revokes the grant while the tutor's 15 tutored channels are live, or any transient stream fault) -- so that one channel goes permanently dark for the rest of the session, with zero AppLogger entry, zero Crashlytics record, and no resubscription, while sibling channels keep working. evidence.quote: awk -F: '{match($$1, /features\/([^\/]+)\//, a); match($$0, /features\/([^\/]+)\//, b); if(a[1] != b[1]) print}'
awk -F: '{match($$1, /features\/([^\/]+)\//, a); match($$0, /features\/([^\/]+)\//, b); if(a[1] != b[1]) print}';

why: The awk derives BOTH the importing-file's feature name and the imported feature name from $0, which is the full grep -rn output line beginning with the FILE PATH — so match($0,...) always finds the importer's OWN feature name (from the path prefix) before ever reaching the import statement, making a[1]!=b[1] always false. recommendation: Fix the awk to extract the imported-feature name from the import-statement TEXT only (e.g. split the grep -rn line on the first ':' twice to isolate the content, or use grep -oP 'features/\K[^/]+' scoped to the substring after the import path's package: prefix) so it stops reading the file-path prefix. title: Make SacredWindowDao's cache replace atomic — clearAll()+insertAll() must be one transaction, not the caller's fire-and-forget chain
why: The DAO's own doc comment says '[clearAll] + [insertAll] are called together... Expects the caller to have called [clearAll] first so the table stays coherent' — but the DAO exposes no atomic way to do that, and the only caller (SacredWindowRepository._persistToDb) chains them with `.then(...).ignore()`: unawaited, no transaction, errors silently discarded. If the process dies (routine on mobile backgrounding) between clearAll() completing and insertAll() completing, sacred_window_entries is left empty. That table is the documented source of truth for 'background notification-fire-time checks... without the Flutter engine' (DNI-367) — an empty table means Sacred Time notification suppression silently fails open on next cold-start check, with no error anywhere (`.ignore()` explicitly suppresses it). invalidate() → _persistToDb runs on every location/timezone change and app resume, so the window isn't rare.
recommendation: Add a single `SacredWindowDao.replaceAll(List<SacredWindowEntriesCompanion> entries)` that wraps clearAll+insertAll in one `db.transaction()`, and have sacred_window_repository.dart call that instead of the `.then().ignore()` chain. If fire-and-forget is intentional, at minimum log the failure via AppLogger instead of `.ignore()`.
acceptance_criteria: SacredWindowDao exposes an atomic replaceAll(); sacred_window_repository.dart no longer calls clearAll()/insertAll() separately.
A test makes insertAll throw mid-write inside replaceAll and asserts the table still holds the PREVIOUS rows (no empty-table window), not a partially-cleared state.

corrections: Downgrade P1 -> P2: the 'silent notification-suppression failure' consequence is aspirational, not live — grep confirms `sacredWindowDao.getAll()` is called nowhere in lib/ outside its own DAO/tests; isWindowActive() only consults the in-memory cache. The DB-2 violation itself (non-transactional, unawaited, .ignore()'d clear+insert) is real and should stay filed, but as design debt tied to the AC-26.24-req-4 background-read feature landing later, not as a currently reachable user-visible defect.

title: Fix unsafe `as int?`/`as num?` casts in TrackCodec.decode and GoalCodec.decode that throw instead of returning null
rule: EH-2/EH-4 decode() null-on-malformed contract + Nygard partial-failure
why: entity_codec.dart's decode() contract states it 'Returns null when required fields are missing or malformed — the merger must skip malformed rows rather than crash.' Every other numeric field read across all 15 files in this batch goes through FirestoreCodec.parseInt, built specifically because Firestore fields can arrive as String (its own docstring says so). These 3 sites bypass it with a bare `as` cast: if profile_id/track_id/target_percent ever arrives as anything but exactly int (or num, for target_percent)/null — e.g. a String from a hand-edited doc, an import script, or a legacy document — `as int?`/`as num?` throws instead of returning null. TrackConfigMerger.merge() and GoalMerger.merge() call `_codec.decode(row)` inside a `for` loop with no try/catch, and MergeRouter.dispatch (merge_router.dart:55) awaits merger.merge() with no try/catch either, so one malformed row throws out of the whole pull page mid-iteration, silently dropping every row after it and aborting the sync pass instead of just skipping the bad row.
recommendation: Replace `raw['profile_id'] as int?` / `raw['track_id'] as int?` with `FirestoreCodec.parseInt(raw['profile_id'])` / `FirestoreCodec.parseInt(raw['track_id'])` (the int.tryParse fallback lines become redundant and can be deleted). Add a `FirestoreCodec.parseDouble` helper mirroring parseInt and use it for GoalCodec's target_percent instead of the raw `as num?` cast.
acceptance_criteria: Unit test: TrackCodec().decode({'profile_id': '5', 'track_id': '7', 'curriculum_id': 'x', 'activated_at': <iso>}) returns a TrackRow, not a thrown exception.
Unit test: GoalCodec().decode({...,'target_percent': '55'}) returns a GoalRow with targetPercent 55.0 instead of throwing.
grep for 'as int?' / 'as num?' / 'as double?' / 'as bool?' across lib/core/sync/codec/*.dart returns zero matches (wire into make audit).

The GoalCodec.decode() citation (goal_codec.dart:77) is misleading: GoalMerger.merge() does NOT call `_codec.decode(row)` at all — GoalCodec.decode() is dead code, never invoked in production (only GoalCodec.encode() is used, for push). Net effect: the defect class is real and reachable for goals too, just at a different, uncited file/line than claimed; the fix recommendation (patch GoalCodec) would not actually fix the live goal bug. The TrackCodec evidence (2 of 3 cited sites) is fully solid and independently sufficient to uphold at P1.

Site 3 (goal_codec.dart:77) is not reachable the way the finding describes. GoalMerger.merge() never calls GoalCodec.decode() — it has its own independent, equally-unsafe cast at goal_merger.dart:91 (`(row['target_percent'] as num?)?.toDouble() ?? 100.0`), which IS reachable via the same unguarded merge-loop/pull-abort chain as the track_codec sites. title: Guard stage_definition/settings/goal merges against missing local track before FK-constrained insert
rule: Nygard (I/O ordering race) — FK integrity on merge; matches the fix already applied to bookmark/gamification_settings/study_day_config
why: lib/core/database/tables/stage_definitions.dart and goals.dart both declare `trackId => integer().references(CurriculumTracks, #id)()` — a real, enforced FK. If a stage_definition/settings/goal Firestore snapshot merges before its curriculum_tracks row exists locally (independent per-collection listeners, or first-launch pull on a restored device), the raw insert throws an uncaught SqliteException(787) and aborts merging the whole page. BookmarkMerger (drift_merge_store.dart:527 `if (track == null) { ...skip... }`), GamificationSettingsMerger (gamification_settings_merger.dart:128 `if (localTrack == null) continue;`) and StudyDayConfigMerger (study_day_config_merger.dart:66 `if (trackExists == null) continue;`) already guard this exact race by skipping and relying on the next (idempotent) pull to re-merge — the pattern was never generalized to stage_definition/settings/goal, which resolve the identical remote-track-id-fallback (`localTrack?.id ?? remoteTrackId`) without ever checking the fallback actually exists.
recommendation: Add the same trackExists-before-insert guard (skip, don't throw; rely on idempotent re-merge next pull) to DriftMergeStore._upsertStageDefinition, _upsertSettings, and GoalMerger.merge, mirroring StudyDayConfigMerger's existing pattern.
acceptance_criteria: Integration test: merge a stage_definition (and separately a settings, and a goal) row referencing a curriculum_id with no local curriculum_tracks row yet — assert no exception is thrown and the row is silently skipped.
Same test seeds the track afterward and re-merges the identical row — assert it now applies (idempotent recovery).
New regression tests live under test/core/sync/merge/, mirroring the FK-race coverage style already present for bookmark/study_day_config.

corrections: The finding understates that this is already partially bounded: sync_orchestrator.dart wraps every pull step (`step()` at ~L759, `log()` in `_buildRecoveryPullTriggers` at ~L1449) and the real-time listener dispatch (`_onListenerEvent` at ~L1373 `.catchError(...)`) in outer catch-alls that log-and-swallow local DB errors, so this does NOT crash the app or abort other collections' sync — it's non-fatal and self-heals (tracks are pulled before stage_definitions/goals in the launch-pull step order, so a full relaunch/resume pull resolves it). The real, still-valid defect is coarser-grained: one bad row in a listener snapshot or pull page currently drops the *entire* batch of legitimate stage_definition/goal/settings rows for that dispatch, not just the offending row — exactly the failure mode the sibling per-row guards were added to prevent. Recommendation and acceptance criteria remain correct as written.

The finding's phrase 'uncaught SqliteException(787)' is uncaught only at the merger/router level - sync_orchestrator.dart:~780 has a defense-in-depth catch (_isLocalDatabaseError) that swallows it per-step, logs 'sync_pull_step_db_error_nonfatal', and lets the sync session continue, so this does not crash the app or abort the whole session, only that one step's page for that cycle (self-heals next pull). Severity/verdict unaffected.

title: Fix StudyDayConfigMerger to use DriftMergeStore.remoteIsNewer instead of the pre-Phase-3 merge_rules.remoteIsNewer
rule: FB-2 (server-timestamp / clock-skew LWW ordering, never client-clock-only)
why: Every other LWW merger in this batch (bookmark, track_config, settings, stage_definition, learning_order, profile_program, goal, learner_profile, gamification_settings, notification_settings, ui_preferences — 11 of 12 natural-key/singleton mergers) was upgraded in the documented 'Phase 3' pass to call `_store.remoteIsNewer`, which adds the ±5s clock-skew window plus Firestore server-timestamp (synced_at) tie-break specifically to fix FB-2's 'faster clock always wins' problem (see drift_merge_store.dart:34-38, 111-152, including the D15 fix). StudyDayConfigMerger alone still calls the plain free function from merge_rules.dart, which has neither: it is a strict `remoteUpdatedAt.isAfter(localUpdatedAt)` with no skew tolerance and no server-timestamp fallback. A device whose clock runs even a few seconds fast will have its study-day-config edits always win the comparison, silently discarding a genuinely newer edit made on a second device.
recommendation: Give StudyDayConfigMerger a MergeStore dependency (constructor param, like every sibling merger) and call store.remoteIsNewer with the row's synced_at; drop its import of merge_rules.dart.
acceptance_criteria: Unit test: two devices' clocks 3s apart, both writes inside the ±5s window, no synced_at on one side — StudyDayConfigMerger resolves identically to DriftMergeStoreTest's D15 clock-skew group, not via strict remote.isAfter(local).
grep confirms study_day_config_merger.dart no longer imports the free-function remoteIsNewer from merge_rules.dart.

title: Move _decodePayload() calls inside outbox_processor.dart's per-row try blocks so one bad payload can't abort the whole drain

evidence.quote:
// Continue draining other rows — don't abort the whole batch on
          // a single failure.

why: _decodePayload throws FormatException when a row's payload isn't a JSON object (DB corruption, a future write bug, or jsonEncode(null)). Both call sites sit OUTSIDE any try/catch: line 292 is inside the eligibleCompletions loop before the try at line 306, and line 383 is immediately before the per-row try at line 384. A single malformed row therefore throws all the way out of _drainForProfile → _doDrain → drain()'s try/finally (the finally still clears the single-flight guard, but nothing catches or converts the error), skipping every other pending completion, every remaining non-completion kind, AND the profile-0 account sweep in _doDrain — on every one of the 5 wired drain triggers, forever, until the row is fixed out of band. This directly contradicts the code's own stated invariant quoted above.
recommendation: Wrap each _decodePayload call in its own try/catch (or catch FormatException specifically) so a bad payload is treated like any other per-row failure: logged, markAttempted (or immediately dead-lettered, since it can never succeed), and does not block sibling rows or other kinds.
acceptance_criteria: Regression test: insert one outbox row with a non-JSON-object payload (e.g. payload: 'null') alongside a valid row of a different kind; drain() must not throw, the valid row must still be pushed, and the bad row must be marked attempted without blocking siblings.
Same test repeated for a malformed completion-kind row.

corrections: The EH-2/EH-3 rule citation is only loosely accurate — the raw exception IS caught and logged one layer up in sync_orchestrator.dart (satisfying EH-3's catch/log requirement and EH-2's presentation-boundary requirement), so this is better framed as a reliability/per-row-isolation defect (violates the file's own stated invariant) than a strict EH-2/EH-3 hit. title: Add ref.mounted guards and Timer disposal to SignInController's autoDispose async flows

evidence.quote:
final watchdog = Timer(const Duration(seconds: 15), () {
      if (state is SignInSubmitting) {

why: This 1016-line Notifier<SignInState> is registered autoDispose and performs 84 awaited operations per file (multi-second retries, 8s Firestore timeouts, 350ms polling loops) yet contains zero occurrences of 'mounted' anywhere in the file — every method touches `state`/`_ref` after an await with no disposal guard. If the user backs out of the sign-in screen mid-request (a completely ordinary action while a 'signing in...' spinner shows), autoDispose tears the notifier down; when the pending await resolves and the code does `state = SignInError(...)` or `_ref.read(...)`, Riverpod 3 throws UnmountedRefException. The watchdog Timer compounds this: it is only cancelled in signInWithEmail/signInWithGoogle's own `finally` block, never via ref.onDispose, so if the notifier is disposed mid-flight the Timer keeps running and fires `state = ...` against an already-disposed notifier up to 45s later. The codebase already has an established ref.mounted convention elsewhere (dashboard_providers.dart, notification_providers.dart, sacred_location_provider.dart all use it), so this file's total omission is an inconsistency, not a repo-wide non-issue.
recommendation: After every await that precedes a `state =` or `_ref.read(...)` write, add `if (!ref.mounted) return;`. Register `ref.onDispose(watchdog.cancel)` immediately after each Timer is created (both the 15s and 45s watchdogs).
acceptance_criteria: A notifier test that disposes the ProviderContainer (or pops the route) while signInWithEmail/signInWithGoogle is mid-await asserts no exception escapes and no post-dispose state write occurs

title: Stop achievementsOverviewProvider and _pointConfigDataProvider writing to Drift/SharedPreferences and pushing to Firestore from inside FutureProvider build
rule: SM-2 (provider build is pure: no writes/requests/side effects)
why: Both providers exist to compute a read-only view model (achievements list / per-track point config rows), but their build functions mutate persisted state (SharedPreferences milestone config, Drift PointConfigs rows) and push a network sync write as an unguarded side effect of simply being watched. title: Add ref.mounted/context.mounted guards after awaits in RewardConfigController and the pending-redemptions fulfil/decline handlers
rule: SM-4 (after any await in a Notifier method/async callback, check ref.mounted before touching ref/state)
why: RewardConfigController is an autoDispose Notifier (confirmed via reward_config_controller.g.dart: isAutoDispose: true) whose saveReward/toggleEnabled/deleteMilestone/_persistAndSync methods each await one or more DB/network calls and then read `state` or call `ref.invalidate`/`ref.read` afterward -- with zero ref.mounted checks anywhere in the file (grep confirms). If the user saves/toggles/deletes and the screen is popped (e.g. the success dialog's own navigation, or a fast back-gesture) before the await resolves, Riverpod 3 throws when a disposed Ref is touched. The same shape recurs in parent_pending_redemptions_screen.dart's _fulfil/_decline: `ref.invalidate` runs BEFORE the `context.mounted` check that appears one statement later in the same function -- the check exists, it's just ordered too late. By contrast, every other async flow in this exact feature (child_redemption_screen.dart, achievement_unlock_celebration.dart, reward_configuration_screen.dart) consistently checks mounted immediately after every await, so this is a real, demonstrated-known-pattern that these two files skip. corrections: The finding's "unhandled Future error" framing slightly overstates the silence: main.dart's runZonedGuarded + PlatformDispatcher.instance.onError DO catch this and route it through AppLogger.instance.handle() and Crashlytics (as a misleading fatal report), so it isn't fully log-less. But this doesn't rescue the finding: there's still no retry/reconciliation, no user-facing signal, and no test exercises the failure branch — the core defect (silent, permanent loss of the siyum credit with zero test coverage of the failure path) stands.</evidence_correction>

Severity should be downgraded from P1 to P2. The finding's "why" claims the failure would be "silently" absorbed with "no user-facing signal" and "no reconciliation job anywhere in lib/ to catch the gap." This overstates the risk: main.dart wraps app startup in runZonedGuarded (lines 15-34), and an uncaught error from an unawaited Future is delivered to that zone handler, which calls both `_crashlytics.recordError(error, stack, fatal: true)` and `AppLogger.instance.handle(error, stack)`. So the exception is NOT silent — it is logged and reported fatal to Crashlytics, giving operators a signal (though not an automatic retry/reconciliation for the missed siyum credit). The rule citations (EH-2/EH-3) are also a loose fit: EH-3 concerns log-less *catch blocks*, and there is no catch block here at all; EH-2 concerns raw exceptions propagating into *presentation*, which doesn't happen since the zone handler intercepts before reaching UI. The underlying gap — no explicit local handling/retry for this specific invariant (B1 siyum credit) and no test exercising the failure path — is real design debt (P2: "design debt with stated concrete cost"), not the P1 "silent, unsignaled defect" the finding portrays.

The finding's framing of 'no user-facing signal' is accurate, but 'silently fails' slightly overstates the logging gap: main.dart wraps the app in runZonedGuarded, whose handler does route unhandled Future errors to AppLogger.instance.handle(...) and Crashlytics.recordError(fatal: true) — so the exception is NOT unlogged. This doesn't kill the finding: the underlying invariant break (siyum permanently not recorded, no retry, no scoped/contextual handling) is real and untested, which the finding's own recommendation and acceptance criteria already account for (explicitly asking for a catch path 'instead of relying on the global zone error handler').

title: Guard ref.mounted after await in SacredLocationNotifier/InIsraelNotifier mutator methods
why: detect() awaits a GPS fix with a 15-second timeout then unconditionally writes state/invalidates ref on success; setManualCity, setManualCoords and InIsraelNotifier.setInIsrael likewise touch state/ref after an await with no ref.mounted check. This file's own _load() methods DO guard (comment: 'an account switch rebuilds it. Never write state on a disposed notifier'), and the paired test file carries a regression test titled 'was a race' proving the team already hit a real race in this exact provider once. If the notifier is disposed while one of these four unguarded methods is mid-await (profile/account switch during a slow GPS fetch is the obvious trigger), Riverpod 3 throws UnmountedRefException, which nothing in the call chain catches (the caller's try/finally in sacred_time_settings_card.dart has no catch clause).
recommendation: Add `if (!ref.mounted) return;` immediately after every await in detect(), setManualCity(), setManualCoords(), setInIsrael(), and _pushSnapshot() before the next ref/state touch, mirroring the guard already used in _load().

title: Scope DataExportImportService.importData()'s 16 bare table deletes to the imported profile, not every profile on the device

evidence.quote:
/// Per-profile import: deletes all existing rows and re-inserts from the
  /// export payload. Does not hard-delete accounts not present in the export

why: Every delete in importData() (lines 517-532, one per user-data table) calls Drift's `delete(table).go()` with no `.where()` clause, which executes an unconditional DELETE FROM on that table. On a device with more than one local account or learner profile (the app's own account-switcher/registry and sibling-profile model), importing ONE profile's exported JSON silently erases every OTHER profile's/account's rows in all 16 tables first -- directly contradicting the method's own doc comment. The multi-account round-trip test (epic_26_story_23_data_export_round_trip_test.dart) can't catch this because it manually wipes the ENTIRE database before calling importData(), so a scoped delete and this unscoped one are indistinguishable to that test. DataExportImportService has zero production callers today (grepped repo-wide across lib/), so no user is exposed yet, but it is fully implemented and covered by ~900 lines of tests across 8 test files -- clear signal a 'restore backup' UI hookup is imminent, at which point the first restore on a multi-child/multi-account device would silently erase a sibling's entire Torah-study history.
recommendation: Thread profileId/accountId into importData() and scope every delete with `..where((tbl) => tbl.profileId.equals(profileId))` (account-level equivalent for accounts/learnerProfiles); extend the round-trip test to seed two profiles and import only one.
acceptance_criteria: New/updated test seeds profile A and profile B, exports+imports only A, and asserts profile B's rows in all 16 tables are byte-for-byte unchanged (not just non-empty).

Every _database.delete(...) call in importData() carries a matching .where(...) scoping clause -- checkable by a Rule-0 grep asserting no bare `delete(_database.` call lacks a following `..where(` in this file.

title: Log and surface the swallowed exceptions in step_starting_position.dart._loadContent and step_starting_position_calendar.dart._refreshCalendarEntry instead of silently stranding the user
why: step_starting_position.dart._loadContent catches everything and only flips _loading to false — it never logs via AppLogger and never sets an error flag. Since _containers/_leaves default to [], build() falls straight through to `_buildContainerList` with an EMPTY list and no CircularProgressIndicator, no error text, and no retry action: the user lands on a blank, silently-broken 'starting position' step of the Add-Track wizard with the Continue button permanently disabled (onPressed requires _selectedLeaf != null, which can never become non-null from an empty list) and zero indication anything went wrong. step_starting_position_calendar.dart._refreshCalendarEntry has no catch at all (only `finally`) around two awaits, and every caller invokes it via `unawaited(...)`, so a thrown exception becomes an unhandled Future rejection with no AppLogger trail; the user instead sees the ALSO-hardcoded 'No local calendar entry found for this date.' fallback, which mislabels a real fetch/service failure as 'no data for this date'.
recommendation: In both catches (or the missing one in the calendar file), log via AppLogger with context (curriculumId/programKey), and expose a distinct error state to the widget (e.g. an AppErrorView with retry, matching the pattern TrackManagementBody already uses via ref.watch(...).when(error: ...)) instead of silently falling through to an indistinguishable empty/fallback UI.
acceptance_criteria: Both catch paths call AppLogger.error/warning with the caught exception before updating state.
A widget test that makes the repository/service throw asserts a visible error affordance (not a blank list / not the generic 'no entry' text) appears.
EH-3's log-less-catch grep (once made a checker) passes on both files.

corrections: Site 2's claim of 'no AppLogger trail' is not accurate: main.dart wraps runApp in runZonedGuarded(), whose handler calls AppLogger.instance.handle(error, stack) (and Crashlytics.recordError) for any uncaught zone error, which includes unhandled Future rejections from unawaited(_refreshCalendarEntry()). So the exception IS logged globally, just without curriculumId/programKey context and without any widget-local error state — the user still only ever sees the hardcoded 'No local calendar entry found for this date.' fallback (confirmed at line ~426), which is the real, narrower defect at this site. Also note _refreshCalendarEntry has no catch block at all (only finally), so it isn't literally an 'empty/log-less catch' under EH-3's wording — the recommendation to 'log via AppLogger in both catches' requires adding a catch clause here, not fixing an existing one. Keep the finding but drop the 'no AppLogger trail' claim for site 2 and center it on 'misleading UI fallback + no contextual/local error surfacing', not a literal EH-3 catch-block violation.

Site 2 claim "a thrown exception becomes an unhandled Future rejection with no AppLogger trail" is inaccurate: main.dart's runZonedGuarded error handler calls AppLogger.instance.handle(error, stack) (and Crashlytics.recordError fatal:true) for any unhandled zone error, which includes errors from unawaited(_refreshCalendarEntry()) since it has no local catch. The defect at site 2 is better framed as: missing contextual (curriculumId/programKey) logging and a misleading generic fallback UI, not a total absence of logging. Site 1's claims are all verified accurate as written.

Site 2's premise is partly wrong: step_starting_position_calendar.dart's _refreshCalendarEntry has try/finally with no catch, called via unawaited(...), so any thrown exception propagates as an uncaught zone error — but main.dart wraps runApp in runZonedGuarded whose handler calls `AppLogger.instance.handle(error, stack)` (main.dart:32) and reports to Crashlytics. So the finding's claim of 'no AppLogger trail' for site 2 is factually incorrect — it IS logged, just not surfaced as a distinct UI error state (the misleading 'No local calendar entry found for this date.' text remains a real but separate UX issue, weaker than an EH-3 log-less-catch violation since there's no catch block at all here). The finding should stand on site 1 alone; site 2 / the 'sites: 2' framing and its EH-3 rationale should be dropped or reframed as a UX-only concern in any rewrite.

title: Stop LearningOrderRepositoryImpl.getOrder from writing to the DB as a side effect of a FutureProvider build call
rule: SM-2 (provider build is pure — no writes/side effects)
why: getOrder is invoked directly from learningOrderProvider's FutureProvider.family build callback, yet it performs a DB write (_stampReorderAt) whenever the stored learningOrderVersion is stale — and nothing else ever updates learningOrderVersion except an explicit user reorder/reset. So on every cold start or provider invalidation while the version mismatch persists, merely reading the curriculum's order silently re-stamps lastReorderAt = now, which is exactly the reorder-amnesty trigger — overdue-item detection for that curriculum stays silently suppressed after any content reseed until the user happens to manually reorder or reset, defeating a named product invariant via a function that looks like a pure read.
recommendation: Move the version-mismatch re-amnesty write out of getOrder into an explicit, one-shot repair step (run once at app start or as part of the content-reseed pipeline) so provider build stays a pure read.
acceptance_criteria: Test: call getOrder() twice in a row with a stale learningOrderVersion and assert lastReorderAt is stamped at most once, not on every call

title: Check TutorGrantResult before treating revoke/resign/rescind as successful in manage_tutors_screen.dart and manage_grants_screen.dart
why: All three handlers await the use case's Future<TutorGrantResult> and discard the return value, then unconditionally run the success branch (wipe local mirror, invalidate the grant list, send a lifecycle email) inside `if (mounted) { ... }`, with only a generic `catch` around thrown exceptions. title: Point epic_27_integration_lockout_redaction_atomic_test.dart AC3 at CompletionRepositoryImpl instead of a hand-rolled transaction
rule: TQ-8 (regression test must exercise the source; FR20 named invariant)

  // is *outside* the transaction — DNI-385 ratifies the invariant the wire-up

title: Rebuild TrackLearningOrderScreen's masechtos ReorderableListView with a lazy builder, not shrinkWrap+children

evidence.quote:
static bool hasReorderableLevel2(CurriculumId id) =>
      id != CurriculumId.chumash && id != CurriculumId.tanach;

why: Track Detail's 'Reorder Learning Order' tile (track_detail_screen.dart:642-658, one tap: `onTap: () => Navigator.of(context).push(MaterialPageRoute(builder: (_) => TrackLearningOrderScreen(...)))`) opens a screen whose masechtos section renders one DraggableOrderItem (a ListTile wrapped in ReorderableDragStartListener, itself a ConsumerWidget with its own label-provider watch) per distinct level-2 hierarchy value of the track's curriculum, via the plain (non-.builder) ReorderableListView constructor with shrinkWrap:true nested inside a SingleChildScrollView. hasReorderableLevel2 enables this section for every curriculum except Chumash/Tanach. I counted distinct level-2 values directly from the bundled assets/content/hierarchy/*.json: Mishna Berurah=697 (Simanim), Mishneh Torah=85, Mussar=59, Mishnayos=63, Yerushalmi=39, Bavli=37. Any user with one of these active tracks — the majority of the app's curricula — who taps 'Reorder Learning Order' forces the screen to synchronously build and lay out every one of those rows in one frame: shrinkWrap:true requires the sliver to size itself before the outer SingleChildScrollView can lay out, so simply swapping to `.builder` without also removing shrinkWrap would not fix it. This is the most severe PF-2 site found in this pass: worst-case count (697) is the highest found, per-item cost is heavier than a bare ListTile, and it is reached by an ordinary, one-tap, documented user action on ordinary curricula (not an edge case).
recommendation: Replace `ReorderableListView(children:...)` with `ReorderableListView.builder(itemCount: _localMasechtos!.length, itemBuilder: ...)`, and remove the shrinkWrap:true + SingleChildScrollView nesting — host the sedarim and masechtos sections in a single CustomScrollView with SliverReorderableList sections (or SliverList for read-only rows) instead, so the shrinkWrap-forced full eager layout is eliminated along with the eager builder.
acceptance_criteria: Rule-0: PF-2 checker (grep/custom_lint) flags `ReorderableListView(` (non-.builder) combined with `shrinkWrap: true` anywhere under lib/features/**.

Regression test: pump TrackLearningOrderScreen for a Mishna Berurah track backed by a 700-item trackMasechtosOrderProvider fixture; assert via find.byType(DraggableOrderItem) that only a viewport's worth of rows are realized (not all 700), and that tester.pumpAndSettle completes within a bounded frame budget instead of timing out.

title: Lazy-load GroupedDailyView's per-curriculum task list instead of List.generate-ing every DailyTaskCard
why: SchedulerScreen's grouped view (one tap on the view-toggle button next to the task count) renders every task for every curriculum synchronously: GroupedDailyView maps curricula (bounded, <=9) into always-expanded ExpansionTiles, and inside each tile calls `List.generate(tasks.length, ...)` to build one DailyTaskCard per task with zero windowing, inside a non-builder `ListView(children:...)`. The daily-task backlog is explicitly unbounded by design — a lapsed user (the app's own core scenario: a child who stops opening the app for weeks) accumulates overdue new-learning/chazara items across every active track. The Learn tab already anticipates exactly this by hard-capping its own preview to `tasks.take(5)` (learning_screen.dart:346) and linking its 'View all' button straight into this screen (SchedulerRoute). Opening the grouped view after a multi-week gap forces dozens of DailyTaskCard widgets (icons, badges, InkWell, Riverpod watches) to build on the main isolate in a single frame — visible jank or a frozen scroll, worst on the older/budget Android devices this app targets for children. The file's own sibling `_TaskList` in scheduler_screen.dart:210 (the default, non-grouped view of the SAME data) already solves the identical problem correctly with `ListView.builder(itemCount: tasks.length, ...)`, so this is a local inconsistency/regression, not an unknown gap.
recommendation: Rebuild GroupedDailyView on a CustomScrollView: one SliverToBoxAdapter per curriculum for the expand/collapse header, followed by a SliverList(delegate: SliverChildBuilderDelegate(...)) (or a lazily-built ListView per expanded section) so only on-screen DailyTaskCards are realized — mirroring the SliverList/SliverChildBuilderDelegate pattern gamification_screen.dart already uses for its own (also unbounded) achievements list.

Regression test: pump SchedulerScreen with a fixture of ~200 synthetic overdue DailyTasks spread across 3 curricula, switch to grouped view, and assert via find.byType(DailyTaskCard) that only the initial viewport's worth of cards are realized (matching the count already asserted for the compliant _TaskList path) rather than all ~200.

Strengthens the finding: the claim 'daily-task backlog is explicitly unbounded by design' understates the mechanism — only the chazara/review sub-path is capped (kMaxOverdueChazarahPerDay=20 in scheduler_engine.dart); the overdue/today projection path that dominates allDailyTasksProvider (scheduler_providers.dart _buildProjectionTasks, ~lines 691/890) has no cap whatsoever, making the worst case larger than the original finding implied.

title: Route LearningLedgerCodec.encode's completedAt through FirestoreCodec.encodeDateTime instead of raw toIso8601String()
rule: Evans consistency (single documented UTC-safe conversion path) / data-integrity
why: Every other DateTime field in all 14 sibling codecs — and every other field in this very file (see decode() at line 84-86) — is pushed via FirestoreCodec.encodeDateTime, which forces `.toUtc()` before serializing so the wire string always carries a 'Z' suffix. This one call skips it. entry.completedAt is read back from Drift's `dateTime()` column which, per the pinned drift-2.31.0 source (lib/src/runtime/types/mapping.dart:174, default storeDateTimesAsText=false, not overridden anywhere in this repo), decodes via `DateTime.fromMillisecondsSinceEpoch(unixSeconds*1000)` with no isUtc:true — producing a **local**, non-UTC-flagged DateTime even though the original value came from DateTimeFactory.nowUtc(). `.toIso8601String()` on a non-UTC DateTime omits the 'Z'/offset entirely. When a different device (a parent or tutor on a different device/timezone — an explicitly supported flow in this app, see tutor_grant_codec.dart in this same batch) pulls the row, FirestoreCodec.parseDateTime's `DateTime.tryParse(raw)?.toUtc()` (used by learning_ledger_merger.dart) reinterprets the offset-naive string using the READING device's local offset rather than the writer's, shifting completedAt by the delta between the two devices' UTC offsets — potentially moving a ledger entry onto the wrong calendar day on the syncing device.
recommendation: Change line 67 to `'completed_at': FirestoreCodec.encodeDateTime(model.completedAt),` to match every sibling codec.
acceptance_criteria: Regression test: encode a LearningLedgerRow with a non-UTC-flagged completedAt (isUtc:false, simulating the Drift round-trip) and assert the resulting 'completed_at' string ends in 'Z' and represents the correct UTC instant.

title: AuthStateNotifier._init() must guard reloadCurrentUser() so an offline cold start cannot hang the session state forever

evidence.quote:
if (firebaseUser != null) {
      final refreshed = await authRepo.reloadCurrentUser();

/// App has not yet resolved the initial session (splash window).
  /// Must not hang — see 19.6 startup hardening.

why: FirebaseAuthGatewayImpl.reloadCurrentUser() calls User.reload(), a network round-trip that throws FirebaseAuthException(network-request-failed) when offline — an entirely ordinary cold-start condition for an offline-first app (this exact file set otherwise engineers carefully around it, e.g. sign_in_controller.dart wraps every Firestore/Firebase call in try/catch and timeouts). Nothing in AuthStateNotifier._init() catches this; the exception escapes the fire-and-forget call from build(), so `state` never advances past AuthState.initializing(). AuthGuard never touches Firebase and lets onboarded users straight through to the app shell, which reads authStateProvider downstream — so a returning cloud-born user opening the app with no connectivity can be stuck on an unresolved session state indefinitely, directly violating the SessionStatus.initializing doc comment's own 'must not hang' contract (a lesson the codebase already learned once for the router guard per the '19.6 startup hardening' reference, but that didn't carry over to this newer Notifier-based path).
recommendation: Wrap the Firebase-touching logic in _init() (at minimum the reloadCurrentUser() call) in try/catch; on failure, fall back to trusting the cached bare currentUser or the local-born row rather than leaving state unset, mirroring the defensive timeout/try-catch pattern already used elsewhere in sign_in_controller.dart.
acceptance_criteria: Regression test: mock AuthRepository.reloadCurrentUser() to throw (simulating an offline reload()), build AuthStateNotifier, and assert state resolves to a terminal SessionStatus within a bounded time instead of remaining initializing indefinitely.
On-device check: cold-start the app in airplane mode with a previously-active cloud-born session and confirm no indefinite splash/loading hang.

corrections: The cited rule AU-4 is misapplied. AU-4's actual text/Why ("Gate startup/session routing on authStateChanges()/idTokenChanges() streams, never a bare currentUser read... currentUser can be null before auth finishes initializing (startup race)") addresses a different defect: using authRepo.currentUser (a bare synchronous read, which _init() also does at line 31) instead of subscribing to the auth-state stream. It says nothing about catching exceptions from reload()/network calls. The defect this finding actually demonstrates — an unhandled exception escaping an unguarded async call and permanently stalling state — is better characterized as an EH-2 violation (raw exception not converted to a value at the data boundary) or filed as a standalone violation of the in-code 'must not hang' invariant, not AU-4. Severity P1 is still justified independently via the digest's 'violated named invariant' clause, and the recommendation (wrap in try/catch, fall back gracefully) is sound regardless of the rule mislabel — but the ticket's rule tag should be corrected before filing.

AuthGuard (learning_tracker/lib/app/router/guards/auth_guard.dart) never reads authStateProvider/Firebase — it only checks SharedPreferences onboarding flags and a local DeviceRegistryDatabase, so it does not gate on session state and there is no confirmed navigation/splash hang. SessionStatus.isInitializing is unused in all production code (grep confirms only its own definition and one unit test reference), so nothing currently blocks/waits on it. The actual confirmed consequence is silent downstream misbehavior in currentAccountIdProvider (falls back to profileId 1), autoSelectedProfileId (returns null), RestoreGuard.hasCloudAccount, and app_shell's offline-banner/upgrade-nudge logic — not an indefinite UI hang. Rule citation AU-4 is a loose fit; EH-2/EH-3 (uncaught exception not converted to a value at the boundary) better describes the mechanism, though the bare `authRepo.currentUser` read at line 31 is a genuine literal AU-4 violation worth folding in.

The finding frames the bug as contingent on 'if a Firebase Auth SDK bump changes the exception's string format.' title: Wrap LearningLedgerRepositoryImpl's ledger insert and outbox enqueue in one transaction
why: recordCompletion inserts the learning_ledger row (line 104) and then enqueues its outbox row (line 127) as two separate, unwrapped statements; recordCompletionsBatch commits all N ledger rows inside one _database.transaction() (closes at line 195) but then loops the outbox enqueue afterward, outside that transaction, one row at a time. A process death or crash between these steps leaves a ledger entry (e.g. a manual siyum mark from the Lifetime Marking screen) permanently local-only — nothing re-derives a missing outbox row from an existing ledger row, so it never reaches Firestore or a second device. The sibling CompletionWriter (completion_writer.dart) explicitly wraps its analogous completion_events + outbox insert in one Drift transaction for exactly this reason (its docs call this 'Both rows commit or both roll back' — the FR15/RC1 fix); LearningLedgerRepositoryImpl doesn't follow the same discipline for the same class of append-only sync-critical data.
recommendation: Move the outbox enqueue for recordCompletion inside the same transaction as the ledger insert (or into one atomic Drift batch, as CompletionWriter does); for recordCompletionsBatch, move the per-item enqueueLedgerEntry calls inside the existing transaction block instead of running them afterward in a separate loop.
acceptance_criteria: Both recordCompletion and recordCompletionsBatch write the ledger row(s) and their outbox row(s) inside one transaction; a regression test that fails mid-batch (e.g. a Fake outbox facade that throws after N/2 calls) asserts no ledger row survives without a matching outbox row.

corrections: New evidence beyond the finding: lib/core/database/daos/outbox_dao.dart:11-12/19-20 states insertOutboxRow 'must be called inside the same transaction as the triggering write' — a directly-named invariant, stronger grounds than DB-2 alone. Also: local_data_upload_service.dart:255-259 does re-enqueue every ledger row, but only as a one-time local-to-cloud cutover bridge (story 19.7), not an ongoing safety net — the 'nothing re-derives' claim holds for steady-state usage.

title: Guard inviteTutor against silently resetting an already-active tutor grant

evidence.quote: //   1. Validate preconditions against the local [TutorGrant] aggregate.

why: grantId is deterministic ({encodedEmail}__{parentUid}__{childProfileId}), so a second inviteTutor call for the same tutor+child pair overwrites the same doc unconditionally, even when the existing grant is currently 'active'. That silently resets state back to 'pending', issues a fresh invite_token/expires_at, and replaces permissions with the request-supplied defaults (which include can_bulk_prior_completion: true) -- while the already-active tutor_active_access index doc is untouched, so the tutor keeps live read access even though tutor_grants.state now says 'pending'. Neither the Cloud Function nor the Dart InviteTutorUseCase (whose own docstring claims it validates against the local grant aggregate, but whose implementation only validates email format) guards against this, so a parent re-sending an invite, or a duplicate form submission, can silently re-grant a permission the parent had explicitly turned off.
recommendation: Before writing, read the existing grant (if any) and reject/short-circuit re-invites while state === 'active' (direct the caller to a permission-editing flow instead), or explicitly preserve prior permissions and keep tutor_active_access consistent with the resulting state.
acceptance_criteria: A new cf_grant_invite.test.mjs test: inviteTutor called twice for the same tutorEmail+childProfileId while the grant is 'active' does not silently reset state/permissions.

corrections: manage_tutors_screen.dart:284-286: the 'Invite a tutor' button is always visible per child section, with an explicit comment 'so the parent can add a tutor even when one is already active,' and the screen has no check against re-entering an existing tutor's email. This confirms normal one-tap navigation (not just double-submit/network-retry) reaches the silent-reset path described, and it silently re-applies default permissions (including can_bulk_prior_completion:true) that may override ones the parent had deliberately disabled -- a user-visible, reachable defect against the named invariant that active grants aren't silently reset, warranting P1 over the originally-filed P2.

title: Fix TutoredPullService.pull()'s misleading on-Exception comment / uncaught upsert failure

title: Guard FirebaseAuthGatewayImpl link/reauth methods against silent no-op on null currentUser

Every sibling precondition check in this same file (deleteCurrentUser:172-176, updatePassword:181-186, reauthenticateWithEmail:192-199, sendEmailVerification:100-104) throws `StateError` instead of silently no-op'ing; the one genuinely-intentional no-op in the file (`updateDisplayName`) is declared as such by an explicit 'is a no-op when no user is signed in' test — these three methods have neither the guard nor a test declaring the no-op intentional, which is the tell that it's an oversight, not a design choice.

Add regression tests mirroring the existing 'throws when no user is signed in' pattern for linkWithGoogleIdToken, linkWithEmailAndPassword, and reauthenticateWithGoogleIdToken.

The 3rd (reauthenticateWithGoogleIdToken) is live but its only real call path guarantees currentUser is non-null, and the downstream deleteCurrentUser() call already guards null with a thrown StateError, so the claimed silent-orphan-account scenario has no actual path through the app today. title: Wrap DeviceRegistryDatabase.removeAccount's delete + state-clear in a transaction()

evidence.quote:
for (var i = 1; i < group.length; i++) {
        removed += await removeAccount(group[i].accountId);

why: removeAccount's own docstring says it clears lastActiveAccountId 'so the next launch does NOT silently auto-activate an arbitrary fallback account against a dangling pointer (D10)' — but the delete and the pointer-clear are two separately-awaited statements with no db.transaction() around them. If the process dies between them (routine on Android when a backgrounded app is reclaimed, and account removal is exactly the kind of action a user triggers then backgrounds), the delete commits but the clear never runs, leaving deviceState.lastActiveAccountId pointing at a row that no longer exists — the exact D10 state device_registry_test.dart's 'removeAccount clears it when removing the ACTIVE account (D10)' test checks for, just reached through a crash path the in-memory test can't simulate. dedupeByEmail compounds this by calling removeAccount N times in an unwrapped loop, so a mid-run crash also leaves a partially-merged duplicate-account state. Every other multi-write DAO in this codebase (stage_dao.dart, curriculum_scope_dao.dart, user_profile_dao.dart, track_dao.dart, points_balance_dao.dart) wraps its writes in transaction() — this file is the outlier.
recommendation: Wrap removeAccount's body in `await transaction(() async { ... })`; wrap dedupeByEmail's per-group removal loop in one enclosing transaction (or a single batched delete) so a crash mid-merge can't leave a partially-deduped state.

DB-2's Pending checker (audit grep for ≥2 awaited writes with no enclosing transaction() in a DAO method body) returns zero for this file.

corrections: Third evidence line cites device_registry_database.dart:185 but the quoted two-line snippet actually starts at line 184 (`for (var i = 1; ...)`) with line 185 being the second line only — off-by-one, not load-bearing.
