title: Guard AuthStateNotifier._init() against I/O exceptions so auth state never hangs at AuthState.initializing() forever

evidence.quote:
if (firebaseUser != null) {
      final refreshed = await authRepo.reloadCurrentUser();

/// App has not yet resolved the initial session (splash window).
  /// Must not hang — see 19.6 startup hardening.

why: build() kicks _init() fire-and-forget and returns AuthState.initializing() immediately; _init() then awaits 4+ Firebase/DAO calls (reloadCurrentUser, findCloudBornByFirebaseUid, getUserProfileByFirebaseUid, upgradeLocalToCloud, findByTier) with zero try/catch anywhere in the method. AuthState has exactly 3 statuses (initializing/signedOut/signedIn) — there is no error state — so any exception during _init() (a DB read failure, a Firebase reload throwing) is an unhandled Future rejection that leaves sessionStatus permanently stuck at `initializing`. This directly contradicts the domain model's own doc comment: 'Must not hang — see 19.6 startup hardening.' Every screen gating on authStateProvider (router, app_shell, sign-in flows) would show a permanent splash/loading state with no retry path, recoverable only by force-killing the app. EH-1's global PlatformDispatcher.onError would log the exception, but nothing resets `state`, so the hang persists regardless of logging.
recommendation: Wrap _init()'s body in try/catch (or convert the class to a plain function-style Future<AuthState> build via AsyncNotifier<AuthState> + AsyncValue.guard); on any caught exception, log via AppLogger and fall back to `state = const AuthState.signedOut()` rather than leaving `initializing` unresolved.
acceptance_criteria: _init() cannot leave sessionStatus at initializing on any exception path — it resolves to signedIn or signedOut every time, with the failure logged via AppLogger.

Regression test: override authRepositoryProvider/userDatabaseProvider with a fake that throws from reloadCurrentUser() (and separately from the DAO) during _init(); assert authStateProvider settles to a terminal state within the test, not stuck at initializing.

Rule-0 checker: none exists yet; add a heuristic grep/custom_lint (once custom_lint is unbroken) flagging a Notifier's build() that calls an unawaited private async method with zero try/catch in that method's body.

corrections: Cited rule SM-5 governs AsyncValue<T>-typed provider state (AsyncLoading/AsyncValue.guard) and explicitly bans manual try/catch state assignment; AuthStateNotifier's state is a custom AuthState (not AsyncValue), confirmed by auth_state_provider.g.dart:28 (`$NotifierProvider<AuthStateNotifier, AuthState>`). Correct citation is SM-2 (build must be pure/no side effects — build() kicks _init() fire-and-forget). The finding's primary recommendation (manual try/catch assigning state) contradicts the very SM-5 clause it invokes; only its parenthetical AsyncNotifier+AsyncValue.guard alternative is actually SM-5-compliant.

isInitializing (auth_state.dart:75) is never read by any router guard or screen except its own domain test — confirmed by grep across app/router/**, features/**/screens/**. This contradicts the finding's 'permanent splash/loading state ... recoverable only by force-killing the app' claim. Also: rule citation SM-5 is a misfit — SM-5 governs AsyncValue<T>-based AsyncNotifier mutations ('let build throw; never hand-manage loading/error with try/catch that assigns state'), but AuthStateNotifier's state is a plain custom AuthState (not AsyncValue), and the finding's own recommendation (add try/catch, manually assign state) is the literal opposite of what SM-5 mandates. EH-2 ('raw exception must never propagate into presentation... convert to a value at the data-layer boundary') is the better-fitting rule for this defect.

The claim 'every screen gating on authStateProvider ... would show a permanent splash/loading state' is false: `AuthState.isInitializing` (auth_state.dart:75) has no callers in lib/ — no widget, guard, or splash screen branches on SessionStatus.initializing. All real consumers (app_shell.dart:140,152,453; profile_providers.dart:23,79; auth_guard.dart) read isSignedIn/isCloudBorn/currentUser, which are identical for initializing and signedOut states, so a failed _init() silently degrades to signed-out-equivalent behavior rather than hanging any UI. Recommend re-filing at P2 citing SM-2 (side-effectful build) rather than SM-5, with corrected consequence: silent session-restore failure treated as signed-out, not a permanent splash/force-kill hang.

title: Move TextContent/TextSegment out of text_cache_repository.dart (data layer) into domain/entities/ so presentation and its tests stop importing the data layer
rule: Presentation→data import ban [P]; naming/placement (domain models belong in domain/); Evans lens (bounded-context leak)
why: TextContent/TextSegment are plain immutable data holders — exactly what domain/entities/ is for (that directory exists, scaffolded with a lone .gitkeep, but was never populated) — yet they are defined at the top of text_cache_repository.dart, the DATA-layer repository implementation. That forces text_display_screen.dart (presentation, and a churn HOTSPOT at 1028 lines) to import the data layer just to type its own widget fields (_TextContentView.textContent, _NumberedSegmentColumn.segments). recommendation: Create lib/features/content_browsing/domain/entities/text_content.dart holding TextContent/TextSegment (mechanical move, no behavior change). Update text_cache_repository.dart and text_display_screen.dart (+ its tests) to import the new domain file instead of the repository file.

title: Wire RewardConfigController's async mutations to the RewardForm.loading/.error fields the screen already renders
why: RewardForm carries loading/error fields and reward_configuration_screen.dart fully renders them (full-screen CircularProgressIndicator for form.loading, a dedicated error Scaffold for form.error) — but grep-confirmed, the controller's 4 async mutation methods (saveReward, toggleEnabled, deleteMilestone, milestonesForCurrentLadder) never set either field to a non-default value anywhere in the file; only bootstrap() touches them, always resetting to false/null. The screen's own try/catch only catches TutorWriteException per call site (for the tutor-permission-denied case). Any OTHER DB failure during a save/toggle/delete (constraint violation, disk error) is an unhandled Future rejection: the user taps Save, sees no spinner (loading never flips true) and no error (error never gets set) — the operation silently fails with zero feedback, while the fully-built error UI remains permanently dead code.
recommendation: In each of the 4 mutation methods, set `state = state.copyWith(loading: true)` before the DB call and wrap it in try/catch: on success `loading:false`; on any exception (not just TutorWriteException) `state.copyWith(loading:false, error: <mapped message>)`, or migrate the class to expose `AsyncValue<RewardForm>`-style guard semantics.

Widget test: a fake RewardMilestoneService/DB that throws a generic exception from upsertMilestone; assert the screen renders the form.error branch instead of hanging or throwing past the test.

refutations: Evidence checks out (grep-verified: none of saveReward/toggleEnabled/deleteMilestone/milestonesForCurrentLadder ever set loading/error; screen catches only TutorWriteException at 3 call sites). But this duplicates an already-filed, UPHELD main-sweep finding: verified-findings-r3.json 'Delete or wire
corrections: No factual error in the cited evidence — form.loading/form.error are confirmed dead (only bootstrap() touches them) and the 4 async mutations are confirmed to lack try/catch beyond the screen's TutorWriteException-only wrappers. The defect is real; the problem is novelty/duplication and severity calibration relative to the already-filed twin P3 finding, not correctness of the grep evidence.

Site count should be 3 real mutation methods (saveReward, toggleEnabled, deleteMilestone), not 4 — milestonesForCurrentLadder is a read-only query consumed by a separate widget-local FutureBuilder and structurally cannot/should not be wired to form.loading/form.error without causing a UX regression (whole-form spinner over a small list refresh). The recommendation's primary fix (manual try/catch assigning state) contradicts the literal SM-5 text cited as the rule; genuine SM-5 compliance requires migrating to AsyncValue<RewardForm>, offered only as a secondary 'or' in the recommendation.

Two corrections: (1) Rule fit is weak — SM-5 mandates AsyncValue.guard and explicitly forbids "hand-manage loading/error with a try/catch that assigns state," yet the finding's own primary recommended fix (wrap each method in try/catch, `state.copyWith(loading:..., error:...)`) is exactly that forbidden pattern; EH-2 ("no raw exception reaches presentation") fits the actual defect better than SM-5. (2) "sites: 4" overcounts: milestonesForCurrentLadder is a pure read consumed via independent FutureBuilder (manage_rewards_list.dart / _InlineRewardsSection), never wired to RewardForm.loading/error by design — only saveReward/toggleEnabled/deleteMilestone are genuine instances of the described root cause (3 sites, not 4). title: Cache the account list Future instead of constructing it fresh inside AccountPickerScreen.build()
why: registry.getAllAccounts() is called directly inside `Widget build()`, which returns a brand-new Future object on every rebuild. recommendation: Hoist the fetch behind a FutureProvider/AsyncNotifier (e.g. deviceAccountsProvider watched via ref.watch), or convert to ConsumerStatefulWidget and cache the Future in State so its identity is stable across rebuilds.

title: Replace fixed Future.delayed sleeps with a deterministic await in scheduler provider tests
rule: TQ-6 (hermetic tests, no timing-based synchronization) / Fowler flaky-test smell
why: Every one of these sites follows the same pattern: `c.listen(skippedTasksProvider, (_, __) {})` then a hardcoded 100-200ms sleep, hoping SkippedTasks._loadFromPrefs() (fired via `unawaited()` inside build()) finished first — instead of awaiting the load itself, because the notifier exposes no future to await. Under a loaded CI runner or slower SharedPreferences-mock resolution the guess can be wrong: assertions then run against the stale initial `{}` state, or (in the several tests that call `.skip()`/`.undoSkip()` immediately after the sleep) a late-resolving `_loadFromPrefs()` can overwrite `state` with old prefs data right after the test's own mutation, silently clobbering it. The result is an intermittent, hard-to-reproduce CI failure with no diagnostic pointing at the real cause, plus 3+ seconds of pure sleep time paid on every run across these 4 files.
recommendation: Give SkippedTasks a way to be awaited deterministically (e.g. an internal `Future<void>` the notifier tracks that a test helper can await via `container.read(...notifier).debugReadyForTest`), or restructure as an AsyncNotifier so tests can `await container.read(skippedTasksProvider.future)`. Replace all fixed-delay call sites with that await.
acceptance_criteria: No `Future<void>.delayed` remains in test/features/scheduler/presentation/providers/*.dart used purely to wait for provider initialization.
A test that artificially slows the fake SharedPreferences resolution (e.g. via a delayed Future in the mock) still passes, proving synchronization is no longer time-based.

title: Delete or rewrite the 474 row-existence-only Drift Manager-API tests in test/core/database/user_database_managers_*_test.dart — none can detect an ordering or filtering regression
rule: TQ-8 (tautological tests / assertions weaker than what the source can do wrong) + Feathers lens (test has no seam to the behavior it claims to cover)
area: test/core/database (Drift generated Manager API coverage tests)

evidence.quote:
/// OrderBy + filter coverage for all remaining uncovered ColumnOrderings and
/// ColumnFilters getters in user_database.g.dart.
// createdAt defaults to currentDateAndTime; just verify the filter compiles and executes

/// Additional coverage for annotation composer getters that were missed in
/// the first computed fields test — focuses on fields like id, profileId,

/// Coverage for annotation composer ($$XxxAnnotationComposer) getters
/// in user_database.g.dart.

why: Every one of these 474 tests inserts exactly one row in setUp, then calls orderBy/filter/computedField/withFields and asserts only `hasLength(1)`/`isNotEmpty`/`isA<List<...>>`. Confirmed by exhaustive grep: zero occurrences anywhere in the 2435-line orderby file of `hasLength(0)`, `hasLength(2)`, or `equals([...])` — no test ever inserts a second, differently-ordered or non-matching row, so a broken `.asc()`/`.desc()` (or a filter predicate that matches everything, or one that silently no-ops) still returns the single seeded row and the test stays green. Ran both the smallest (crossref_filter_test.dart) and largest (orderby_test.dart) files in this session: 26/26 and 283/283 pass today, so this is 474 currently-green CI checkmarks that give zero regression protection for the very ordering/filtering behavior their names promise. Compounding it: `grep -rl '\.managers\.' lib/` returns 0 files — the Drift-generated Manager API under test (`db.managers.*`) has no caller anywhere in production code; the app queries through hand-written DAOs instead. This is ~5900 lines of test code (this batch alone) written to drive `flutter test --coverage` numbers up against a generated-code surface the app never exercises, at real cost: CI/build time on every run, and reviewer/agent attention budget on every future change to user_database.dart (per AG-3's own rationale about per-file read budgets).
recommendation: Delete this suite — `db.managers.*` has no production caller, so there is no behavior left to protect. If the underlying goal was raising `user_database.g.dart` line-coverage numbers, exclude generated files from the coverage gate instead (e.g. `lcov --remove coverage/lcov.info '*.g.dart' '*.freezed.dart'` in the coverage make target) rather than writing assertion-free tests. If any ordering/filtering behavior here genuinely needs protecting because a DAO wraps it, move that coverage to the DAO's own test file with real assertions: insert ≥2 rows with distinct sort keys and assert exact order via `equals([...])`, and insert ≥1 matching + ≥1 non-matching row per filter test and assert the non-matching row is excluded.
acceptance_criteria: `grep -rn 'db.managers' test/core/database/user_database_managers_*_test.dart` returns nothing (files deleted), OR every remaining orderBy test seeds ≥2 rows with distinct values and asserts exact order, and every remaining filter test seeds ≥1 excluded row and asserts it's excluded.
Coverage tooling (`make test` / CI) excludes `*.g.dart` and `*.freezed.dart` from the coverage report, removing the incentive that produced this suite.
`flutter test --coverage` line count for `test/core/database/` drops by roughly the amount removed, verifiable via `wc -l` before/after in the PR diff.

evidence.quote: Direct string comparisons (`profile.mode == 'child'`) should be replaced

why: account_tier.dart's own docstring names exactly this anti-pattern as the W5.11 sweep target, yet the primary caller of DeviceRegistryDatabase.updateAccountTier (the local→cloud upgrade flow) hardcodes the raw literal 'cloudBorn' at all 4 of its call sites instead of using AccountTier.cloud.storageKey — the read path (DeviceAccountX.accountTier) already goes through the typed enum, so write and read now use two unlinked representations of the same key. Separately, profile_model.dart re-implements ProfileMode's string↔enum mapping with its own switch (silently defaulting to adult) instead of calling ProfileMode.fromStorageKey (which throws on unrecognized values). Neither currently misbehaves — the literals happen to match — but a typo or a future storage-key rename in the VO would not be caught by the compiler at any of these 5 sites, and the two ProfileMode mappings already have different error-handling semantics (throw vs. silent default) for what is meant to be the same conversion.
recommendation: Replace the 4 'cloudBorn' literals with AccountTier.cloud.storageKey; have profile_model.dart's profileMode getter delegate to ProfileMode.fromStorageKey (wrapped in the same kind of fail-safe try/catch pattern already used in child_mode_guard.dart) instead of re-switching.
acceptance_criteria: upgrade_to_cloud_service.dart contains zero raw 'cloudBorn'/'localBorn' string literals; all go through AccountTier.*.storageKey.
profile_model.dart's profileMode getter calls ProfileMode.fromStorageKey (or documents why it deliberately diverges).

corrections: profile_mode.dart quote is at line 11, not 10. upgrade_to_cloud_service.dart 'cloudBorn' lines are 183/222/325/362, not 183/221/324/361 (3 of 4 off by one).

title: Adopt or delete 6 of 7 unused NaturalKey.forX factories — mergers duplicate the exact key-format logic inline

evidence.quote: /// [DriftMergeStore] splits on `|` to decode composite keys, so the

why: The file's own doc comment claims these factories 'replac[e] ad-hoc `$a|$b` string concatenations that were scattered across the merger layer' — but a repo-wide grep of lib/ and test/ shows forTrackConfig, forStageDefinition, forSettings, forBookmark, forLearningOrder and fromSingle all have zero callers; only forCompletion is used (1 call site, in completion_event_merger.dart). The mergers still hand-roll the identical shapes instead: core/sync/merge/stage_definition_merger.dart:48 builds `'${decoded.curriculumId}|${decoded.trackId}|${decoded.stageOrder}'` by hand — the exact 3-column shape forStageDefinition exists for — and core/sync/merge/learning_order_merger.dart:35 does the same for the 2-column shape forLearningOrder exists for. Because DriftMergeStore decodes these keys by splitting on `|` (the documented invariant at line 13-14), the format is load-bearing for sync correctness but is maintained by convention across 8+ merger files instead of the one factory meant to own it — a future edit to one merger's key shape without updating the others would silently break natural-key matching (double-inserts or dropped LWW comparisons) with no compiler check to catch the drift.
recommendation: Either route the unused-factory mergers (stage_definition, settings, track_config, bookmark, learning_order) through the matching NaturalKey.forX calls, or delete the unused factories and correct the misleading doc comment. Prefer adoption since it centralizes the `|`-separator invariant DriftMergeStore depends on.
acceptance_criteria: Every core/sync/merge/*_merger.dart natural-key construction calls a NaturalKey.forX factory, or the doc comment at natural_key.dart:9-11 is corrected to stop claiming repo-wide adoption

A regression test asserts NaturalKey.forStageDefinition/forLearningOrder produce the exact strings the mergers currently hand-build, so a future format change breaks loudly in one place instead of silently

corrections: All 7 natural_key.dart quotes are exact and grep confirms only forCompletion has a caller; the other 6 are dead. Independently found 4 more mergers (bookmark/profile_program/settings/track_config_merger.dart) hand-rolling the identical single-column shape, corroborating the duplication claim beyond what the finding cited. However the 'why' chain's claim that 'DriftMergeStore splits on `|` to decode composite keys' does not hold: drift_merge_store.dart and sync_kv_dao.dart contain no `.split('|')` call anywhere — naturalKey is used only as an opaque SyncKv equality key, never decoded. That specific mechanism is stale/inaccurate (inherited uncritically from the source file's own doc comment), but the core dead-code + cross-file duplication claim is independently confirmed and still supports P2.

title: Route UserProfileHeaderCard through feature barrels instead of 6 deep cross-feature imports; settings.dart barrel is dead (Rule 2)

evidence.quote: // Import this barrel (features/settings/settings.dart) from outside this

why: Rule 2 requires cross-feature references go through a barrel; UserProfileHeaderCard instead reaches directly into 3 files under features/account and 3 under features/profiles. Meanwhile features/settings/settings.dart -- the feature's only declared public surface, per its own header comment -- exports nothing and a repo-wide grep shows zero files import it. This is invisible in the audit baseline because the Makefile's own Rule-2 checker (make audit check 15/15, learning_tracker/Makefile:374-386) is broken: its awk step compares the feature name parsed from the file-path column against the feature name parsed from the FIRST 'features/X/' match in the whole grep line, which is always the importing file's own path (it appears before the import statement in `grep -n` output) -- so a[1] always equals b[1] and the WARN branch can never fire, for any file, repo-wide. I confirmed this by running the exact Makefile pipeline against this file: it produced zero matches despite the 6 genuine cross-feature imports above. Concrete cost: renaming/restructuring AppUser, AuthState or ProfileModel inside account/profiles breaks this widget with no barrel boundary to absorb the change, and nothing in CI would warn about it even though Rule 2 is nominally 'enforced'.
recommendation: Either populate settings.dart (and account's/profiles' equivalents) with a real public surface and route UserProfileHeaderCard's imports through them, or delete the dead settings.dart if the barrel convention is being abandoned. Separately, fix the awk field-comparison in Makefile check 15/15 so it diffs the importing file's own feature (from the path column) against the feature parsed specifically from the `package:learning_tracker/features/...` import string, not the first match in the whole line.
acceptance_criteria: make audit check 15/15 flags a deliberately-reintroduced cross-feature deep import in a scratch file (proves the checker actually fires)
user_profile_header_card.dart imports account/profiles symbols only via their barrels, or settings.dart is removed if the barrel convention is dropped

corrections: coding-standards.md's actual Rule 2 text names `providers.dart` as the sole sanctioned barrel, not `<feature>.dart` — settings.dart is not really 'the' correct target either. Also verified account.dart (populated, real exports) and profiles.dart (empty, like settings.dart) both have zero repo-wide importers too — the dead-barrel problem is systemic across features, broader than the single file reported, not narrower. This strengthens rather than weakens the finding.

title: Wrap the unguarded SharedPreferences/service writes in 9 plain-value Notifier mutation methods across 6 files
area: core/preferences, features/notifications, features/sacred_time, features/scheduler, features/tracks/setup, features/onboarding (presentation/providers)

evidence.quote:
state = value;
    await _writeAndPushSnapshot(ref, pref, profileId, value);

final prefs = await SharedPreferences.getInstance();
    await prefs.setBool(

final prefs = await SharedPreferences.getInstance();
    await SacredTimePreferences.writeLocation(prefs, loc);

final prefs = await SharedPreferences.getInstance();
    await prefs.setStringList(_skippedRefsKey, state.toList());

if (scopeJson != null) {
      final list = jsonDecode(scopeJson) as List<dynamic>;

why: The identical idiom repeats across 9 Notifier classes in 6 files: the class holds a plain-value (non-AsyncValue) state type, an async mutation method optimistically assigns `state` (or navigates state via copyWith), then `await`s a persistence/service call (SharedPreferences write, step.save(ref), jsonDecode of stored JSON) with NO enclosing try/catch anywhere in the call chain. Concretely: (1) preference_providers.dart's 5 `set()` methods and notification_providers.dart's 5 `toggle()`/`setTime()` methods write to SharedPreferences after already showing the new value — a write failure is an unhandled Future rejection and the change is silently lost, reverting on next launch with zero explanation to the user who believed they had already saved it; (2) sacred_location_provider.dart's detect()/setManualCity/setManualCoords/setInIsrael have the same gap, with the added wrinkle that a lost write means the in-Israel/location flag used for Sacred-Time window calculations silently reverts; (3) scheduler_providers.dart's SkippedTasks.skip/undoSkip repeat it despite the SAME file's _loadFromPrefs() correctly demonstrating the fix (full try/catch + AppLogger.error) two methods away; (4) add_track_controller.dart's _advance()/goBack() fire `_persist()` without await or unawaited(), and tryRestore() runs jsonDecode on stored JSON with no try/catch, so a corrupt or stale-schema persisted wizard state throws uncaught instead of falling back to a fresh wizard; (5) onboarding_controller.dart's init()/advance()/jumpTo() await arbitrary OnboardingStep.save/load(ref) implementations with no error channel at all, and the sole caller (learning_process_wizard_screen.dart) does not catch either, so a DB write failure inside any wizard step crashes the flow rather than showing a recoverable error.
recommendation: Introduce a shared helper (e.g. `Future<void> guardedPersist(Ref ref, Future<void> Function() write, {required VoidCallback onFailure})`) that every listed mutation method routes its persistence call through, catching and logging via AppLogger and rolling back or surfacing the optimistic state change on failure; apply it at all 21 sites.
acceptance_criteria: None of the listed methods leaves a bare unguarded `await prefs.setXxx(...)`/`await step.save/load(...)`/`_persist()` (unawaited) as the last unprotected statement of a public mutation method — every persistence call is wrapped in try/catch (or the equivalent AsyncValue.guard) that logs via AppLogger on failure.

Regression test (one representative site per file, full parity recommended): override SharedPreferences (or the relevant service/DAO) with a throwing fake for ShowNikudPref.set, ReminderEnabled.toggle, SacredLocationNotifier.setManualCity, SkippedTasks.skip, AddTrackController's _persist (via goBack()), and OnboardingController.advance(); assert the returned Future does not silently reject unobserved and that in-memory state does not diverge from persisted truth without a logged/surfaced failure.

Rule-0 checker: add a tool/audit grep flagging `Future<void>` methods on `@riverpod`/`Notifier` classes that contain an `await <prefs-or-dao-call>` not preceded by an open `try` earlier in the same method body — a cheap textual first pass ahead of a real custom_lint AST rule.

corrections: add_track_controller.dart's tryRestore() (cited L69) has zero call sites anywhere in lib/ or test/ (grepped repo-wide) — it is dead code, so the jsonDecode-without-try/catch cannot presently throw in production; the _persist()-unguarded claim for the same file via _advance()/goBack() (L188-189) IS reachable and stands. onboarding_controller.dart's init/advance/jumpTo (cited L69) call OnboardingStep.save/load, but all 5 production steps in wizard_steps.dart inherit the no-op default (none override save/load) — 'a DB write failure inside any wizard step crashes the flow' is not yet a live scenario, only latent design debt for a future step. The other 4 files (preference_providers.dart 5 sites, notification_providers.dart 5 sites, sacred_location_provider.dart 4 sites, scheduler_providers.dart 2 sites = 16 sites) are fully confirmed live, reachable, and unguarded, which alone sustains the P2 finding. Rule tag SM-5 is a stretch: SM-5's text bans hand-rolled try/catch *replacing* AsyncValue.guard on AsyncValue-shaped state; these are plain-value Notifiers with NO try/catch at all (the opposite failure mode) — EH-2 ('a raw exception must never propagate') or a Nygard-lens I/O-failure observation is the more precise tag. Also the title's '9' doesn't reconcile with its own 'sites: 21' or the per-file method tallies (5+5+4+2+~3+3 ≈ 21-22) — internally inconsistent count, though immaterial to the underlying defect.

title: Deduplicate 5 shadowed top-level keys in app_he.arb/app_en.arb — one silently kills a zero-task notification branch
rule: Rule 0 gap (no duplicate-key checker for ARB files)
why: JSON's last-key-wins behavior is confirmed against the generated Dart output: lib/l10n/app_localizations_he.dart's todaysLearning(count), errorLoadingTasks(error) and notificationReminderBody(taskCount, curriculumCount) all match the SECOND (later) ARB definition, not the first. No checker anywhere (make audit, arb-parity, flutter analyze) catches a duplicate top-level key within a single ARB file, so 3 of the 5 duplicate pairs carry genuinely different text: an editor who fixes the first (now-dead) copy of todaysLearning or errorLoadingTasks has the fix silently discarded. Worse, notificationReminderBody's line-1765 definition had a deliberately-written zero-task branch (he: 'אין משימות להיום — שמרו על הרצף!' / en: 'No tasks today — stay on track!'); a later duplicate insertion at line 2636/2834 (identical pattern in app_en.arb) replaced it with a two-way plural that has no zero case at all. It is not live-broken today only because the sole caller, lib/features/notifications/presentation/providers/notification_providers.dart:517, has an unrelated 'D2 fix' guard (`if (taskCount == 0) { cancel; return; }`) that happens to prevent taskCount=0 from ever reaching the l10n call — if that guard is ever removed or a second caller is added, Intl.pluralLogic falls to `other` and produces 'You have 0 tasks…' instead of the friendly copy that still sits, unused, in the file. The identical 5-key duplicate set exists in app_en.arb too, confirming this is a systemic missing-checker gap, not a one-off typo.
recommendation: Add a Rule-0 checker (tool/ script or a test/l10n/ test) that fails when any top-level key string appears more than once in app_en.arb or app_he.arb, wired into make audit/ci. Then resolve the 5 duplicates: keep todaysLearning's parameterized form (matches its @todaysLearning metadata), keep errorLoadingTasks's live copy or fix the grammar deliberately, and decide whether notificationReminderBody's zero-task branch should be restored (and its caller's guard removed) or the dead ARB text deleted — don't leave orphaned content either way.
acceptance_criteria: A new checker/test fails when a top-level ARB key is duplicated, and is part of make audit or make ci.
app_en.arb and app_he.arb each contain todaysLearning, errorLoadingTasks, today, notificationReminderTitle, and notificationReminderBody exactly once.
notificationReminderBody's zero-task branch is either wired to a real caller or its vestigial ARB text is removed — no orphaned/unused ICU branch remains.

title: Stop keying GoalEntity.firestoreId on mutable targetPercent — every goal-percent edit orphans a Firestore document instead of updating it
rule: Evans invariant (aggregate identity must be stable across normal mutation); adjacent to the FB family's stable-natural-key principle

evidence.quote: test('two goals with different createdAt have different firestoreIds', () {

why: firestoreId = curriculumId + '_' + targetPercent.toStringAsFixed(1) + '_' + createdAt.millisecondsSinceEpoch. updateGoal preserves createdAt but allows targetPercent to change, so any 'adjust my goal target %' edit (a routine, expected user action) computes a DIFFERENT firestoreId and _syncGoal pushes a brand-new Firestore document instead of updating the original — the original document is never touched again and deleteGoal only ever removes the CURRENT firestoreId's doc, so the old one is orphaned forever. GoalMerger happens to key its LWW arbitration by track_id rather than firestoreId, so the local state pulled on other devices generally self-heals to the latest edit — but Firestore itself accumulates one permanent garbage document per percent-edit for the life of the account, silently inflating every future full pull of that profile's goals collection. The test suite tests firestoreId's format exhaustively (contains curriculumId / contains targetPercent / contains createdAt, in TWO separate near-duplicate files) and even exercises the exact repro (create at 50.0, update to 75.0) but never asserts the one invariant that matters: the id must stay the same across that edit.
recommendation: Derive firestoreId only from fields that cannot change through updateGoal (drop targetPercent from the id, or key on the DB row id / trackId+curriculumId+createdAt) so an update always resolves to the same document.
acceptance_criteria: GoalEntity.firestoreId no longer includes targetPercent (or any other field updateGoal can change).
New regression test: create a goal, call updateGoal changing only targetPercent, and assert the pushed sync payload's id/firestoreId is identical to the create call's.

The confirm-step of `_handleChange` (line 350-351) is worse: it has no try/catch at all around `setProfilePin`, unlike its own sibling handlers. If the provider is invalidated/torn down while a bcrypt hash/secure-storage write is in flight (e.g. rapid navigation away, container disposal), the resulting exception is unguarded and, for the confirm-step case, has no catch clause to even convert it to a value.
recommendation: After each await in _handleSetup/_handleChange/_handleVerify, add `if (!ref.mounted) return;` before assigning state; wrap the confirm-step setProfilePin call in the same try/catch pattern used by _handleSetup.

title: onEnqueueDrain closures in sync_providers.dart read ref after an await with no ref.mounted guard
why: Both onEnqueueDrain closures (in syncWriteFacadeProvider and outboxSyncWriteFacadeProvider) do a ref.read after an await with no ref.mounted check, violating SM-4. Riverpod 3 throws UnmountedRefException if ref is used after its provider has rebuilt. Both providers watch activeProfileIdProvider/authStateProvider, which change on every profile switch or sign-out -- realistic during the network round-trip a drain takes. If that happens between the two awaits, the second ref.read(syncOrchestratorProvider)?.recordDrainAttempt() throws on a stale ref. The surrounding comment (sync_providers.dart:100-104) spells out the user-visible cost of skipping recordDrainAttempt: 'the badge stays at its old value (e.g. a stale Synced) ... a false-Synced when the push failed.' Because this closure runs inside unawaited(tee().catchError((Object _) {})) in outbox_sync_write_facade.dart, the resulting exception is silently swallowed (see the companion EH-3 finding), so this failure currently has zero observability.
recommendation: Check ref.mounted after the first await in both closures before the second ref.read call, per SM-4; extract the duplicated closure body into one shared helper to fix both sites at once.
acceptance_criteria: custom_lint/riverpod_lint rule flagging ref use after an await without a mounted check (SM-4 Enforce backstop).
Provider test that rebuilds/switches the active profile mid-drain and asserts no UnmountedRefException reaches the caller and recordDrainAttempt either completes or is safely skipped.

title: Fix docs/sync-conflict-resolution.md's LWW tie-break rule — it contradicts the implemented and tested behavior
rule: AG-8 (doc/code parity); FB-2/FB-3 (LWW ordering, clock-skew handling)

evidence.quote:
> strictly newer timestamp wins. If both timestamps are equal the remote row
> is silently dropped (the LWW rule is `remoteTimestamp > localTimestamp`).

// The one true tie (equal `updated_at`, no decisive server timestamp) is
    // resolved by preferring remote so two devices that wrote the same value
test('exactly identical timestamps, no synced_at → remote wins', () {

why: The canonical doc says ties are dropped in favor of local (strict `remoteTimestamp > localTimestamp`) and never mentions a clock-skew window. The actual implementation and its exhaustive, intentional test coverage do the opposite for the common case: outside a ±5s skew window ties do stay local, but *inside* the window — the realistic case for near-simultaneous writes from a user's own two devices — an exact tie goes to REMOTE (code comment: 'prefer remote... converge instead of bouncing'), and a `synced_at` server-timestamp tie-break exists that the doc never describes at all. An engineer implementing a new merger or debugging a 'my edit got overwritten' report will read the doc, get the tie-break backwards for the realistic case, and either mis-implement a new merger or chase a phantom bug.
recommendation: Rewrite the 'Push/pull invariant' section to describe the actual 3-tier rule in DriftMergeStore.remoteIsNewer: (1) outside ±5s skew, strict remote>local wins and ties stay local; (2) inside ±5s skew with both sides carrying synced_at, the server timestamp decides; (3) inside the window with no decisive synced_at, remote wins to force convergence. Point the doc at drift_merge_store.dart:113-152 so future changes are easy to diff against it.
acceptance_criteria: docs/sync-conflict-resolution.md's tie-break wording matches lib/core/sync/merge/drift_merge_store.dart:113-152 exactly, confirmed by re-reading both side by side

title: Fix root Makefile's audit/analyze/test-all targets so they stop reporting false passes

evidence.quote:
cd learning_tracker && dart run custom_lint; \
	echo "audit PASSED."

why: The whole `audit` recipe is one shell invocation (backslash-continued); its final two statements are joined by `;`, not `&&`, so the recipe's exit status is that of the LAST command (`echo "audit PASSED."`), never custom_lint's. Empirically reproduced: a `false;`-then-`echo` recipe in a throwaway Makefile prints the trailing text and `make` still exits 0. Since custom_lint is currently broken (crashes, per baseline), running `make audit` from the repo root today prints the crash output and then unconditionally declares "audit PASSED." Separately, root `analyze` omits `--fatal-infos` and `test-all` omits `--coverage`, unlike learning_tracker/Makefile's equivalents (which say "matches CI --fatal-infos flag" and are correct) — so `make ci` from repo root can go green on issues the real CI gate (which always runs from learning_tracker/) would reject.
recommendation: Replace the trailing `;` with `&&` (or check `$?` explicitly) so a lint failure fails the recipe; add `--fatal-infos` to root `analyze` and `--coverage` to root `test-all`, or better, make the root Makefile's targets thin `cd learning_tracker && make $@` wrappers so there is exactly one place these flags can drift.
acceptance_criteria: `make audit` from the repo root exits non-zero when the underlying custom_lint invocation fails.
root `make analyze` uses --fatal-infos and root `make test-all`/`ci` produce coverage output, matching learning_tracker/Makefile.

title: Split allow list from allow read in firestore.rules to cap request.query.limit

evidence.quote: allow read: if isOwner(uid) || hasActiveTutorAccess(uid, profileId);
allow read: if isOwner(uid) || hasActiveTutorAccess(uid, profileId);
allow read: if isOwner(uid) || hasActiveTutorAccess(uid, profileId);

title: Wrap tutorEditProfile's read-then-overwrite in a transaction to stop the lost-update race
why: Every other stateful mutation needing read-then-write consistency in this file (acceptTutorInvite, revokeTutorGrant, resignTutorGrant, expirePendingInvites) wraps it in db.runTransaction. tutorEditProfile instead reads the profile doc, merges edit fields in application memory, then does a full-document `set(..., {merge:false})` with no transaction. If the owner's own device (or a second tutor) writes any other field to the same learner_profiles/{profileId} doc between the get() and the set(), that write is silently overwritten by tutorEditProfile's stale full-doc replace -- a lost-update race, undermining the very H2 fix comment that motivated reading the full doc first.
recommendation: Wrap the read+write in db.runTransaction (txn.get + txn.set), consistent with the rest of the file, or switch to `profilePath.set(updates, {merge:true})` for the scalar fields being edited -- Firestore applies a merge write atomically server-side without a client-side read first.
acceptance_criteria: A concurrency test (a second writer updates an unrelated profile field between tutorEditProfile's get and set) shows that field survives.

title: Make tutor audit-log writes idempotent and failure-visible instead of best-effort auto-ID writes

evidence.quote: /** Write an audit log entry for a tutor mutation (best-effort — errors are logged but not thrown). */

} catch (e) {
    logger.warn(`writeAuditLog: failed for grant=${grantId} action=${action}`, e);

why: The audit log is the parent's only visibility into what an invited tutor did to their child's data (12-month retention, W3.42), but every write to it is swallowed on failure (the primary mutation still returns success:true even if its audit entry silently failed) and keyed by Firestore auto-ID rather than a deterministic key, so a client-side retry of a timed-out-but-actually-succeeded Cloud Function call produces a duplicate entry for the same real action. A parent reviewing the trail can see gaps or phantom duplicates with no way to tell which from inside the app.
recommendation: Derive a deterministic audit_log doc ID from (grantId, action, target, an idempotency key) so retries coalesce, and consider writing the audit entry in the same batch/transaction as the primary mutation so both succeed or fail together.
acceptance_criteria: Calling the same tutor mutation twice with the same idempotency key produces exactly one audit_log entry, proven by a new test.

title: Log the swallowed exceptions in firebase_bootstrap.dart's two comment-only catch blocks (lines 39-41, 50-52) — invisible to the Makefile's single-line-only empty-catch grep

evidence.quote:
} catch (_) {
      // App Check unavailable — continue; sync may be rejected if enforced.

} catch (_) {
    // Firebase init failed — app continues in local-first mode.

why: Both catch blocks have a comment as their only content — no rethrow, no state conversion, no AppLogger call — so they satisfy none of EH-3's three disjuncts ('rethrows, converts, or logs'). This is not merely a Pending-tier gap: the project's own 'Enforced' check for exactly this class of bug (Makefile [9/12], NFR23, 'empty catch blocks catch (_) {}') only matches the single-line literal pattern `catch\s*(_)\s*{}`; running it against this file confirms zero hits despite two genuinely empty-bodied (comment-only) catches spanning multiple lines. The App Check catch (39-41) is the more consequential of the two: the surrounding comment documents a known real failure mode ('FirebearStorageCryptoHelper decryption failures... cause activate() to hang indefinitely') that the timeout specifically guards against, yet if it fires there is zero log trace — this is the same class of App-Check/permission-denied failure this team has separately had to debug via manual token inspection. The outer catch (50-52) swallows a bare (untyped) exception from Firebase.initializeApp() itself with equally zero trace, so a total Firebase-subsystem failure in the field (no sync, no crash reporting, no analytics) would leave no diagnostic breadcrumb anywhere.
recommendation: Change both `catch (_) { /* comment */ }` blocks to `catch (e, stack) { AppLogger.instance.warning(event: '...', exception: e, stackTrace: stack); }` (AppLogger.instance is safe to call here even though AppLogger.init() hasn't run yet — crashlytics_bootstrap.dart already relies on the same lazy-singleton behavior). Separately, broaden the Makefile NFR23 grep so it is not blind to multi-line comment-only catch bodies.
acceptance_criteria: Both catch blocks in firebase_bootstrap.dart (App Check activation, Firebase.initializeApp) capture the exception/stack and call AppLogger.instance.{warning|error} with a distinct event name.

Makefile check [9/12] (NFR23) is extended to also flag catch blocks whose body contains only comments/whitespace, not just literal `catch (_) {}`; re-running it against firebase_bootstrap.dart now reports the two sites instead of 0 hits.
A regression test forces FirebaseAppCheck.instance.activate (or Firebase.initializeApp) to throw and asserts an AppLogger/Talker history entry is recorded.

title: Migrate SignInController's hand-rolled Idle/Submitting/Error state to AsyncNotifier + AsyncValue.guard

evidence.quote:
// DG-GAUTH-01: signInWithGoogle() returned without throwing (no
        // user-cancel / interrupt) but left currentUser null — a silent JWT

why: SignInController extends plain `Notifier<SignInState>` (a hand-written sealed union: SignInIdle/SignInSubmitting/SignInError) instead of `AsyncNotifier<void>`, then hand-manages the loading/error lifecycle with ~15 manual `state = ...` assignments spread across try/catch/finally blocks in signInWithEmail and signInWithGoogle — duplicating exactly what AsyncValue.guard provides for free. This maps cleanly onto AsyncValue<void> (AsyncLoading=Submitting, AsyncData(null)=Idle, AsyncError=Error) but the team hand-rolled it instead. The class's own DG-GAUTH-01 comment documents a previously-shipped bug caused by exactly this pattern: a code path where signInWithGoogle() completed without throwing but left currentUser null previously fell through with 'zero feedback' (state silently stayed at whatever it was rather than transitioning to Error) — proof this hand-rolled machinery has already let a state-transition gap through undetected by the type system. Any new branch added to this 1017-line method carries the same risk; AsyncValue.guard would make 'forgot to set error state' structurally much harder.
recommendation: Migrate to `class SignInController extends AsyncNotifier<void>` (or keep the SignInIdle/Submitting/Error shape but derive it FROM an underlying AsyncValue via a getter) so state transitions on the unhappy path are guaranteed by the framework rather than manually tracked across ~15 call sites.
acceptance_criteria: No code path in signInWithEmail/signInWithGoogle can leave `state` at SignInSubmitting after the method's Future completes (success or failure) — verified structurally by the AsyncNotifier/AsyncValue.guard migration rather than by manual review.

Regression test: extend the existing ensureCloudEmailVerifiedForTest-style coverage with a case asserting that EVERY awaited external call, if it throws, ends in `state is SignInError`/`AsyncError` — not silently at Idle/Submitting.

Rule-0 checker: once custom_lint is unbroken, add a rule flagging hand-rolled sealed `*State` classes with Idle/Submitting/Error (or Loading/Success/Failure)-shaped variants used as Notifier state as SM-5 AsyncNotifier-migration candidates.

corrections: DG-GAUTH-01 comment (L906-910) actually describes a missed postcondition check (googleUser == null after a successful call), not a case where state 'silently stayed' un-transitioned — the prior bug explicitly returned SignInIdle; AsyncValue.guard would not have structurally prevented it since no exception was thrown. Also 'this 1017-line method' is a misnomer — the FILE is 1016 lines; the largest method (signInWithEmail) is ~186 lines. Neither error changes the core verdict: the file, and both target methods, are real, live, and match SM-5's named anti-pattern.

title: Fix ContentTree.parent()'s off-by-one when a leaf precedes its container in source order
rule: Correctness bug (Fowler duplicated-but-inconsistent logic between pass 1 and pass 2)
why: Empirically verified: constructed a 4-level Bavli fixture where the leaf item ('Berakhot 2a:1') appears before its own container ('Berakhot 2a') in the input list, called ContentTree.fromCurricula(...).parent('Berakhot 2a:1'), and got 'Berakhot 2' (the grandparent/daf-level container) instead of the correct immediate parent 'Berakhot 2a'. Root cause: for a leaf, `_ancestorLevels(item)` already returns the PARENT container's own key (that's its documented purpose, and pass 1 at lines 110-121 uses it directly with no further truncation). Pass 2 treats `levels` uniformly as if it were the item's own key and applies a second `.sublist(0, length - 1)` 'walk up one level' step — which, for leaves, walks up an extra level past the true parent. Pass 1 resolves leaves correctly when their container is registered first; pass 2's fallback only fires — with the wrong answer — when a leaf is encountered before its container. recommendation: In pass 2's leaf branch, use `ancestorLevels` (the value already returned by _ancestorLevels) directly as the parent container key, the same way pass 1 does — do not apply an additional sublist(0, length-1) truncation for leaves.

title: Fix mergeCloudPayload treating a non-empty remote payload with a missing/unparseable updated_at as unconditionally newer than local
rule: EH-2 / Nygard lens (LWW ordering must not silently clobber on ambiguous input; mirrors FB-3's null-timestamp guard even though this path is SharedPreferences-based, not core/sync)
why: The short-circuit `remoteUpdatedAt != null && ...` means: when the remote payload is non-empty but its 'updated_at' fails to parse (missing key, malformed string, cross-version format drift), the early-return guard never fires, so the method falls through and unconditionally overwrites local milestones/unlocks with the remote payload -- treating 'timestamp unknown' as 'always newer' instead of the safer 'cannot prove newer, keep local'. This is the exact malformed-timestamp branch never exercised by either reward_milestone_service_test.dart's mergeCloudPayload group (only null/empty/older/newer-with-valid-ISO-dates are tested) or test/sync/merge/gamification_reward_merge_test.dart (same gap, confirmed by grep -- only valid ISO8601 updated_at values appear in that file too).
recommendation: Change the guard so a null/unparseable remoteUpdatedAt is treated as NOT provably newer (skip the merge, same as the older-timestamp branch) rather than falling through to an unconditional overwrite.
acceptance_criteria: mergeCloudPayload with a non-empty milestones/unlocks payload and a missing or garbage 'updated_at' leaves existing local data untouched
A new test in the mergeCloudPayload group covers this exact case and fails against the current code

corrections: Minor: claim that gamification_reward_merge_test.dart has 'only valid ISO8601 updated_at values' is imprecise -- that file never exercises mergeCloudPayload at all (uses a fake callback stub), so reward_settings.updated_at never appears there in any form. Strengthens rather than weakens the zero-coverage claim.

title: Route child_redemption_screen.dart and parent_pending_redemptions_screen.dart error states through AppLocalizations instead of raw e.toString()
rule: EH-5 / AX-2 (no raw exception reaches presentation; everything user-facing via AppLocalizations/ARB) -- matches the currently-non-functional custom_lint rule no_e_to_string_in_ui
why: Both screens render the raw exception's toString() as the entire error-state UI, completely bypassing localization -- in an EN/Hebrew app, a Hebrew-locale user sees untranslated (and potentially technical/internal) English text if the balance or pending-redemptions stream errors. This is not a missing capability: the very same feature already has a sanctioned pattern for this (point_config_screen.dart:222,267 use `AppLocalizations.of(context)!.errorGeneric(e.toString())`, and gamification_screen.dart uses `l10n.errorLoadingCalendar` for its own error states) -- these two sites simply don't use it, an inconsistency within one feature slice.
recommendation: Replace `Text(e.toString())` with `Text(AppLocalizations.of(context)!.errorGeneric(e.toString()))` (or a more specific localized string) in both files, matching the pattern already used elsewhere in the same feature.
acceptance_criteria: Neither file renders a bare e.toString() as UI text; both route through an AppLocalizations-resolved string
A widget test pumps each screen in an error AsyncValue state under Locale('he') and asserts the rendered text is not raw English exception text

title: Add an accessibility label to RewardConfigHeader's icon-only back button
why: The back-navigation IconButton has no `tooltip` and the Icon has no semanticLabel, so a screen-reader user (TalkBack/VoiceOver) reaches this control with no announced purpose — unlike the adjacent PopupMenuButton, which gets a Flutter-provided default tooltip. This is a real, checkable AX-3 gap on a primary navigation control in a screen a parent (potentially using assistive tech) uses to configure rewards.
recommendation: Add tooltip: AppLocalizations.of(context)!.<backButtonLabel> (or reuse MaterialLocalizations back-button semantics) to the IconButton.
acceptance_criteria: A widget test finds a Semantics node with a non-empty label for the back button via find.bySemanticsLabel or tester.getSemantics.

title: Mirror the daily-task-card chevron icon for RTL (Icons.chevron_right_rounded needs matchTextDirection)
rule: AX-3 (directional glyphs mirror in RTL) -- the IL-7 breadcrumb-chevron defect class
why: Icon.matchTextDirection defaults to false and Flutter never auto-mirrors an arbitrary Material glyph; grep -rn matchTextDirection lib returns zero hits anywhere in the app. In the Hebrew (RTL) locale, the Row ambient Directionality already moves these 'go to detail' chevrons to the visual left edge of the daily-task card and curriculum-browse card, but the glyph itself keeps pointing right -- so the arrow points back into the card instead of toward the forward-navigation direction, exactly the defect the standards doc names IL-7 to prevent recurrence.
recommendation: Add matchTextDirection: true to both Icon(Icons.chevron_right_rounded, ...) call sites (or swap to a locale-aware chevron keyed off Directionality.of(context)).
acceptance_criteria: A widget test pumps _LearnTaskCard/_CurriculumBrowseCard at Locale('he') and asserts the chevron Icon has matchTextDirection: true or is rendered horizontally mirrored

corrections: docs/test-artifacts/bulk-fix-plan-2026-06-11.md:342 rates the original IL-7 breadcrumb-chevron defect itself as 'P2' — direct in-repo precedent supporting this defect class's severity.

title: Wire up or delete the unused SharedPrefsNotificationPreferencesRepository

evidence.quote:
/// All key strings and default values are centralised here rather than
/// being scattered across multiple Riverpod notifiers.

why: SharedPrefsNotificationPreferencesRepository is constructed nowhere in lib/ outside its own constructor declaration -- a repo-wide grep confirms zero call sites. Its doc comment claims prefs are centralised here instead of being scattered across notifiers, but every one of the 5 preference providers in notification_providers.dart still reads/writes SharedPreferences key-by-key inline via the static key helpers, exactly the scattered pattern the class claims to replace. It has zero test coverage and misleads a reader into believing there is a repository DI seam here when there isn't one.
recommendation: Either finish the migration (route the 5 providers' load/save through a provider constructing this repository) or delete the class and the interface's now-pointless abstract load()/save(), keeping only the static key helpers that are actually used.
acceptance_criteria: Either a provider constructs SharedPrefsNotificationPreferencesRepository and the 5 notifiers call load()/save() through it with a test exercising both methods; or the class and abstract methods are removed and dart analyze stays clean.

title: Wrap SacredWindowEntries clear+insert in one transaction (DB-2)
why: The table is briefly empty between clearAll() completing and insertAll() starting; neither call is awaited by any caller and neither is wrapped in a transaction. invalidate()'s own separate unawaited clearAll() (line 50) can also interleave with _persistToDb()'s clear-then-insert pair (line 167) in either order. The class's own doc says this cache exists so 'background notification-fire-time checks can read them on cold-start without the Flutter engine' -- a background read landing in the empty gap, or after invalidate() wins a race against a slower insertAll(), sees no Sacred Time windows and could fail to suppress a notification during Shabbos/Yom Tov, the entire point of DNI-367. Confirming the full consequence requires reading the background notification-fire-time isolate handler, which is outside this batch.
recommendation: Wrap clear+insert in one db.transaction(...) and await it from both invalidate() and _persistToDb(), or add an explicit generation-counter guard so a stale clear can't stomp a newer insert.
acceptance_criteria: A DAO-level test that races invalidate() against a concurrent _persistToDb() cycle never observes SacredWindowEntries transition through an empty state once a non-empty write has committed.

title: Test the real _persistNotificationSettingsToCloud signature logic, not a hand-copied reimplementation
why: _persistNotificationSettingsToCloud's M2 no-op-skip logic (skip pushing when the settings signature hasn't changed, to avoid bumping updated_at and clobbering a newer remote under LWW -- the exact mechanism the client-clock finding depends on) is a private function, so G1-G4 reimplement its string format by hand in the test file instead of exercising it. If a future edit to the real signature-building code drops a field or changes the separator, breaking the no-op-skip contract, G1-G4 keep passing because they never call the real function.
recommendation: Extract the signature-building into an internal @visibleForTesting function the tests can call directly, or drive it end-to-end via notificationSettingsCloudSyncEffectProvider with a fake outbox facade asserting enqueue is/isn't called across setting changes.
acceptance_criteria: A mutation check confirms G1-G4 (or their replacement) fail when a field is removed from the real signature-building code in notification_providers.dart.

title: Construct StreakAlertService only through its @riverpod provider (SM-7)
why: streakAlertServiceProvider is locked to activeProfileIdProvider's profile, so allProfilesReminderBootstrap, which must handle every inactive profile, can't use it and hand-constructs a second instance instead. A test that overrides streakAlertServiceProvider with a fake has no effect on inactive-profile scheduling, and any future required dependency added to StreakAlertService's constructor must be kept in sync by hand at both call sites.
recommendation: Convert to a family-style provider parameterized by profileId and use it at both call sites.
acceptance_criteria: A test overriding the family provider for a specific inactive profileId observably changes allProfilesReminderBootstrap's behavior for that profile.

title: Override reminderSyncEffectProvider/streakAlertSyncEffectProvider in notifications_screen_test.dart and ws5_two_layers_test.dart to stop opening a real Drift database
why: NotificationsScreen.build() unconditionally does `ref.watch(reminderSyncEffectProvider)` / `ref.watch(streakAlertSyncEffectProvider)` (both @Riverpod(keepAlive) FutureProviders that chain into notificationSchedulerProvider -> sacredWindowRepositoryProvider -> userDatabaseProvider, i.e. a real drift_flutter-backed UserDatabase opened via driftDatabase(name: 'learning_tracker')). Neither buildSubject() (notifications_screen_test.dart) nor _buildWithProviders() (ws5_two_layers_test.dart) overrides these two effects, unlike the newer notifications_screen_l1_test.dart which does so explicitly "to isolate the UI tests" (its own header comment). Actually running `flutter test test/features/notifications/presentation/screens/notifications_screen_test.dart` reproduces Drift's own runtime warning verbatim: "It looks like you've created the database class UserDatabase multiple times. When these two databases use the same QueryExecutor, race conditions will occur and might corrupt the database" (fires because the file pumps a fresh ProviderScope 5 times against the same default DB name in one process). ws5_two_layers_test.dart pumps the same unguarded path once, so the warning doesn't fire there today, but the identical missing-override defect is present and would manifest the same way if a second pump were added.
recommendation: Add `reminderSyncEffectProvider.overrideWith((ref) async {})` and `streakAlertSyncEffectProvider.overrideWith((ref) async {})` to both builders, matching notifications_screen_l1_test.dart's pattern, so no real UserDatabase/scheduler chain is ever constructed in these widget tests.
acceptance_criteria: buildSubject() in notifications_screen_test.dart and _buildWithProviders() in ws5_two_layers_test.dart both override reminderSyncEffectProvider and streakAlertSyncEffectProvider with no-ops.

Re-running `flutter test test/features/notifications/presentation/screens/notifications_screen_test.dart` prints no "WARNING (drift): It looks like you've created the database class UserDatabase multiple times" output.
(Rule-0, Pending) TQ-6 audit grep: any widget test file that pumps NotificationsScreen must also override both keepAlive sync-effect providers in the same overrides list.

title: Await BulkMarkScreen._expungeRefs's expunge writes before invalidating dependent providers
why: The loop fires expungePriorCompletions (which internally does multiple awaited DB writes) without awaiting it, then immediately calls ref.invalidate on the dashboard/progress providers. Because those providers are manually invalidated rather than backed by a reactive .watch() stream, the invalidated providers can refetch before the un-awaited expunge write lands, showing the user a stale (pre-expunge) completion count right after unticking a previously-marked item. Confirming this needs a widget test with a deliberately delayed fake CompletionRepository asserting the provider's value immediately after _toggleItem completes.
recommendation: await Future.wait(refs.map((r) => service.expungePriorCompletions(...))) before the ref.invalidate calls, or move invalidation into a .whenComplete() continuation.
acceptance_criteria: a test with an artificially delayed expunge write asserts the dashboard provider reflects the post-expunge count immediately after the awaited toggle completes, not the pre-expunge count

title: Populate features/profiles/profiles.dart barrel exports so Rule 2 is satisfiable for the whole feature
why: Every other actually-used feature barrel re-exports its public API (account.dart 21 exports, tracks.dart 26, tutoring.dart 22, progress.dart 1); profiles.dart has zero `export` statements, so its own header comment ('Import this barrel... Do NOT import deep paths directly') is impossible to follow. Grepping lib/features/**/*.dart for `features/profiles/` outside the profiles feature itself finds 65 files across 10+ other features deep-importing active_profile_provider.dart, profile_providers.dart, profile_model.dart, pin_service.dart etc. directly (plus lib/app/router/app_shell.dart, which can't even use the barrel since it exports nothing). Rule 2 is therefore 100% unenforceable for the single most cross-cut feature in the app: any future rename/move inside features/profiles/ breaks an unpredictable subset of 65+ files with no compiler-visible contract boundary.
recommendation: Populate profiles.dart with export statements for the feature's actual public surface (profile_model.dart, profile_repository.dart, pin_service.dart, active_profile_provider.dart, profile_providers.dart, profile_switcher_sheet.dart, etc.), mirroring the structure already used in tutoring.dart, then migrate consumers off deep imports incrementally.
acceptance_criteria: features/profiles/profiles.dart exports every symbol currently deep-imported by 2+ other features

learning_tracker/Makefile check 15/15 (once its self-comparison bug is fixed, see the tutored_children_section.dart finding) shows a declining, tracked count of profiles/ deep imports outside the feature
New cross-feature consumers of profiles/ import only features/profiles/profiles.dart

title: Reuse test/helpers/overflow_harness.dart instead of hand-rolling single-point FlutterError.onError overflow checks in lifetime_folder_styled_and_notif_providers_test.dart
why: coding-standards.md TQ-3 specifies test/helpers/pump_app.dart as 'the reviewed convention' for widget-test pumping, but that file does not exist anywhere in the repo (only an unrelated pumpApp lives in test/e2e/harness/e2e_harness.dart for E2E journeys) — this file's local _wrap/_pump/_tearDown (lines 53-86) is a from-scratch reimplementation. Separately, 6 tests (lines 147, 269, 343, 507, 797, 1146) hand-roll a FlutterError.onError capture to detect RTL overflow at exactly one (size, textScale) point, duplicating and weakening test/helpers/overflow_harness.dart's expectNoOverflowAcrossDevices — an already-adopted (18 call sites), purpose-built matrix checker with a documented central home at test/overflow/overflow_guard_test.dart. The hand-rolled single-point checks in this file cannot catch overflow that only manifests at the tablet width or the 2.0x text-scale corner, which the shared matrix helper is specifically designed to catch.
recommendation: Add the 6 Hebrew-locale/dark-theme cases to test/overflow/overflow_guard_test.dart via expectNoOverflowAcrossDevices instead of the local FlutterError.onError pattern; separately, either build test/helpers/pump_app.dart per TQ-3's spec or point TQ-3 at overflow_harness.dart's _wrap-equivalent so future widget tests have one place to look.
acceptance_criteria: The 6 sites at lines 147/269/343/507/797/1146 are replaced by expectNoOverflowAcrossDevices calls (in this file or test/overflow/overflow_guard_test.dart).
A shared, importable pump helper exists and this file imports it rather than defining its own _wrap/_pump.

title: Remove or wire up the dead MonthlyActivitySliverCalendar spike before its placeholder class collides with the real Drift companion
rule: dead code / AG-4 (future duplicate top-level name)
why: grep across lib/ and test/ shows MonthlyActivitySliverCalendar is imported nowhere except its own file and its own 171-line test (monthly_activity_sliver_calendar_test.dart) — 404 + 171 = 575 lines maintained since commit 2b2eeb54 (2026-05-20) for zero product value; the widget's own doc comment admits 'not wired into any screen yet'. Worse, its hand-rolled `class MonthlyActivityRollup` is explicitly a stand-in 'until build_runner generates the companion' — but the real monthly_activity_rollups Drift table (already committed, not yet added to UserDatabase's table list) declares @DataClassName('MonthlyActivityRollup'), the identical name. The day someone finishes wiring that table into UserDatabase and runs build_runner, this hand-written class and the generated one collide.

No hand-written class reuses a name reserved by a table's @DataClassName annotation

title: Batch trackDualProgressMetricsProvider's per-track sequential DB reads (N+1 left un-fixed by sibling F13)
why: Each loop iteration awaits _safeLoadLeavesForTrack (itself up to 4 sequential DAO calls: getScopesByTrack, getScopes x1-2, getActiveTracksForProfile, lines 618-648), then completionPercent (397), getCompletionsByTrackAndProfile (406), getEntriesByTrack (408), getProgramForProfileAndCurriculum (421), and conditionally programCalendarPositionProvider (430-431) — up to 9 sequential DB round-trips per track, none parallelized via Future.wait. A profile with 5 active tracks does ~40-45 sequential awaits to render the Progress-hub/Dashboard per-track section, and this provider re-runs on every completionCommittedProvider tick (line 357, i.e. after every single completion mark). The very same file already fixed this exact N+1 shape for the sibling lifetimeDataProvider under the F13 label (completionsByProfileForLifetimeProvider / priorImportsByProfileProvider, lines 78-138) but the batching was never extended here. Actual latency impact is unmeasured (SUSPECTED) — the un-batched pattern itself is CONFIRMED by static reading.
recommendation: Batch the per-track queries the way F13 batched lifetimeDataProvider's — one profile-wide query per DAO partitioned in memory by trackId — or parallelize the independent per-track work with Future.wait.
acceptance_criteria: trackDualProgressMetricsProvider issues O(1) queries per DAO (or explicitly parallelizes per-track work), not O(tracks) sequential awaits
A ProviderObserver-based test mirroring lifetime_knowledge_screen_test.dart's F13 test asserts each batched provider builds once across N tracks

title: Move LocationFetchResult out of data/services/location_service.dart so presentation stops importing data/ directly
why: sacred_time_settings_card.dart is a presentation/widgets file; it imports data/services/location_service.dart purely to pattern-match on LocationFetchResult/LocationFetchSuccess/etc. in _showOutcome(). Every other cross-layer type this feature exposes to presentation (City, SacredLocation, SacredWindow) correctly lives in domain/models/ — LocationFetchResult is the one outcome type stranded in data/, forcing presentation to reach past domain into data, breaking the layering the rest of the feature follows consistently.
recommendation: Move the LocationFetchResult sealed hierarchy to domain/models/ (LocationService in data/ still constructs and returns it); presentation then only ever imports domain/ or providers/ from this feature, never data/.
acceptance_criteria: LocationFetchResult and its variants live under domain/
No file under sacred_time's presentation/{screens,widgets}/ imports anything from data/
flutter analyze / make audit stay clean after the move

title: Narrow LocationService's `on Object catch` clauses so programming errors aren't swallowed
why: `on Object` catches everything Dart can throw, including Error subtypes (TypeError, NoSuchMethodError, StateError, ...) that only_throw_errors-compliant code elsewhere in the app throws for genuine programming bugs. A plugin-level type mismatch or null-safety violation inside geolocator/geocoding would silently become 'location fetch failed' (or a silently-null country code) forever, with no crash report and no log line — exactly the bug-masking EH-4 exists to prevent.
recommendation: Change both clauses to `on Exception catch (e)` (or the specific exception types geolocator/geocoding document), letting Error subtypes propagate and reach Crashlytics/crash loudly.
acceptance_criteria: Both catch clauses in location_service.dart are typed to Exception (or narrower), not Object
A test asserts a thrown Error from the fake platform is NOT converted to LocationFetchError/null but propagates

title: Fix ZmanimWindowService polar-fallback candle-lighting/tzais to use the target location's time, not the device's
why: DateTime(y, m, d, 17) (no .utc) constructs a device-local wall-clock time; .toUtc() then converts using the DEVICE's current timezone offset, not the offset of latitude/longitude — an arbitrary location the user picked, which the feature explicitly lets differ from the device's own timezone (manual city/coords). The doc comment above promises 'a wide local-time window' at the target, but the fallback is local to whichever timezone the device (or test runner) happens to be in. It only fires at extreme (polar) latitudes when getCandleLighting()/getTzais() return null, and zmanim_window_service_test.dart has no test forcing that branch, so it has never been exercised.
recommendation: Compute the fallback from a fixed offset derived from longitude (or explicitly switch to UTC and correct the 'local-time' claim in the comment) instead of relying on DateTime's device-local constructor.
acceptance_criteria: Fallback candle-lighting/tzais no longer depends on the executing device's timezone
A unit test at an extreme-latitude fixture forces getCandleLighting()/getTzais() to return null and asserts the returned UTC instant is stable regardless of the test machine's TZ

title: Resolve the ambiguous stageId/stageOrder dual-interpretation in SchedulerCompletionRepositoryImpl.resolveStageOrder
rule: Evans lens — a single field pattern-matched against two overlapping ID spaces with no way to tell them apart

evidence.quote:
final stageOrderMap = {for (final s in stages) s.id: s.stageOrder};
    final knownStageOrders = {for (final s in stages) s.stageOrder};

why: The comment says newer completion rows store a stage's stageOrder in c.stageId while older rows store the stage's DB id; resolveStageOrder tries to guess which format a given row used by checking 'does rawStageId match some CURRENT stage's stageOrder' first. Stage id (a table-wide autoincrement) and stageOrder (a small 1..N per-curriculum ordinal) share the same small-integer space, especially for the first curriculum/stages ever created in a fresh install or test DB (id and stageOrder can be identical by coincidence, e.g. 1,2,3). When they collide, an OLD-format row that really means 'stage id 3' gets misread as 'stageOrder 3' and silently resolves to the wrong stage — which would misreport a chazara/review stage as complete (or vice versa) with no error. I have not constructed a concrete seed scenario proving the collision fires against real data (id values grow globally across curricula, so the window narrows over an install's lifetime), so this is reported as SUSPECTED, not CONFIRMED — a runtime/unit test seeding a stage whose id equals a different stage's stageOrder plus an old-format completion would confirm or rule it out.
recommendation: Give completion rows an explicit format marker (or normalize all stored stageId values to stageOrder in a one-time migration) instead of guessing per-row from an ambiguous value.
acceptance_criteria: A targeted unit test seeds two stages where one stage's DB id equals another (or the same) stage's stageOrder, adds an old-format completion using the id, and asserts resolveStageOrder resolves to the correct stage rather than the coincidentally-matching one.
If the test confirms a collision, resolveStageOrder no longer disambiguates by value coincidence (explicit format tag, or a completed one-time backfill removes the dual-format need).

corrections: Quoted lines are at 37-38 and 43 in current HEAD, not 33/39 as cited — content verified identical, only line offset is wrong (likely stale snapshot vs. a dart-format pass).

title: Populate the scheduler feature barrel (scheduler.dart) with real exports

evidence.quote: // feature. Do NOT import deep paths directly.

why: The entire file is a library declaration plus a comment claiming to be the feature's public surface — it contains zero `export` statements, so importing it gives a consumer nothing usable. Grepping the whole repo confirms no file anywhere imports `features/scheduler/scheduler.dart`; every cross-feature consumer (e.g. lib/core/labels/curriculum_label.dart, lib/core/providers/calendar_providers.dart) is forced into deep imports of internal scheduler files because there is nothing else to import. Once check 15 (see companion finding) is fixed, a grep for `features/scheduler/(?!scheduler\.dart)` from outside lib/features/scheduler/ returns zero matches.
