Also, check-15's awk logic (Makefile lines 374-385) is tautologically broken (always compares a file's own feature name to itself), so the digest's '~32 known baselined edges' is entirely check-14/Rule-1 content, not check-15/Rule-2 — this reinforces rather than undermines the finding's novelty.

title: Normalize config.currentDate before delay-stage due-date arithmetic in SchedulerEngine
why: config.currentDate flows in unnormalized: allDailyTasksProvider sets `now = ref.watch(clockProvider)` (a raw timestamp with time-of-day) and _buildFreshPlan passes it straight through generator.generateAll(activeCurricula, now, ...) -> ScheduleConfig(currentDate: date). previousCompletedAt also carries a real time-of-day (completion timestamps are never normalized — confirmed via completion_writer.dart). Duration.inDays truncates toward zero, so when the true calendar-day gap is exactly 1 day but the elapsed wall-clock time is <24h (e.g. item completed at 20:00 five days ago, now it's 02:00 the next calendar day — only 6h elapsed), daysUntilDue computes 0 instead of -1: a chazara item that is genuinely 1+ calendar days overdue is shown in 'due today' (scheduledTasks) instead of 'overdue' (overdueTasks), silently under-reporting overdue-ness by up to a day. This is the same class of bug (R4-1) this codebase has explicitly fixed elsewhere in the very same feature (local_calendar_engine.dart's UTC-midnight handling, goal_setup_screen.dart's daysRemaining guard, and _buildProjectionTasks's pervasive DateUtils.extractLocalDate use) — just missed in the delay-stage path.
recommendation: Normalize both previousCompletedAt/currentCompletedAt and config.currentDate to calendar-date-only (e.g. via DateUtils.extractLocalDate) before computing daysUntilDue in _processDelayStage, matching the pattern already used in _buildProjectionTasks.
acceptance_criteria: New unit test: a delay-stage item whose previous-stage completedAt time-of-day is later than the current query's time-of-day, with a true 1-calendar-day gap, asserts the task lands in overdueTasks (not scheduledTasks).
scheduler_engine_schedule_types_test.dart / scheduler_engine_dni346_test.dart (sibling test files) continue to pass.

corrections: Rule tag 'DB-6' doesn't match (DB-6 covers sync-able entity local-Drift-as-source-of-truth, unrelated to date arithmetic) — the real grounding is the general date-arithmetic/Nygard clock-skew lens, not a named DB rule. Independently found stronger reachability evidence than cited: chazaraTasks generated via this exact code path are merged into allDailyTasksProvider's effectiveTasks, and CurriculumDefaults.defaultStages applies DelaySchedule(1) (Chazara 1) to every curriculum by default, so this isn't a rare configuration.

title: Move scheduler_providers.dart's projection/plan-building business logic into the domain layer
why: _buildProjectionTasks and _buildFreshPlan are ~200-line pure-ish business-logic functions (amnesty cutoffs, program-vs-self-paced branching, prior-completion filtering) that belong in domain/services or domain/projection — both of which already exist as sibling directories in this exact feature for exactly this purpose. Worse, both functions take `Ref ref` directly as a parameter even though the SAME function signatures already inject `getScopedContent` and `programRepository` as plain callbacks specifically so the logic can be tested without booting Riverpod — the `ref` param undermines that seam (it's used only for one call, `curriculumLabelTextFromRef(ref, curriculum: ...)`, which could equally be injected as a callback like the others). This is why this file is 1381 lines and why testing this logic requires a real ProviderContainer instead of plain unit tests.
recommendation: Extract _buildProjectionTasks/_buildFreshPlan/_applyProgramCalendarOverrides/programCalendarSchedule to a domain/projection or domain/services class; replace the `Ref ref` parameter with a plain `String Function(CurriculumId) trackLabelFor` callback matching the existing DI pattern used for getScopedContent/programRepository.
acceptance_criteria: _buildProjectionTasks and _buildFreshPlan (or their relocated equivalents) take no Ref parameter.
A new domain-layer unit test exercises the amnesty-cutoff and program-vs-self-paced branching logic without a ProviderContainer.
scheduler_all_daily_tasks_test.dart continues to pass unmodified in behavior.

corrections: The evidence array only quotes _buildProjectionTasks's signature (lines 496-497); the parallel claim about _buildFreshPlan (line 940 'required Ref ref,' / line 977 sole use) is asserted in prose but not independently cited — I verified it separately and it holds. Also '~200-line' undersells _buildProjectionTasks, which actually spans ~440 lines (496-935).

title: Guard SkippedTasks.build()'s fire-and-forget prefs load with ref.mounted
why: build() kicks off an un-awaited async side effect (SM-2 forbids side effects in build). _loadFromPrefs() then does `await SharedPreferences.getInstance()` and further awaits before writing `state = ...` twice, with no `ref.mounted` check (SM-4) anywhere in the method. If the provider is disposed (e.g. the user navigates off the Scheduler screen quickly) before the load resolves, the post-await `state = ...` throws Riverpod 3's UnmountedRefException — which the surrounding try/catch swallows and logs via `AppLogger.instance.error(event: 'Failed to load skipped tasks', ...)`, i.e. a routine dispose race gets misreported as a genuine load failure in production logs/Crashlytics breadcrumbs, obscuring real failures of the same code path.
recommendation: Check `ref.mounted` immediately before each `state = ...` assignment in _loadFromPrefs, and return early (without logging) when unmounted, matching Riverpod 3's documented SM-4 pattern used elsewhere in the codebase.
acceptance_criteria: _loadFromPrefs checks ref.mounted before both `state = refs.toSet()` and `state = {}`.
A widget test that disposes the ProviderContainer/screen mid-load does not produce an AppLogger error log.

title: Convert TutorPermissions to @freezed instead of hand-writing ==/hashCode
why: coding-standards.md is explicit: domain value objects must be `@freezed` with generated `==`/`hashCode`/`copyWith`, specifically because hand-rolled equality drifts from the field list. TutorPermissions — its own doc-comment calls it 'Immutable value object' / 'VO' — hand-writes both operators across 9 fields, plus a separately hand-written constructor, copyWith, toFirestore, and fromFirestore: 5 places a future field addition must be updated by hand. The drift risk is already visible today: `canMarkLiveCompletion` is deliberately excluded from both `==` and `hashCode` (harmless only because it is hardcoded false for every instance) — exactly the kind of silent omission @freezed generation would make structurally impossible.
recommendation: Convert TutorPermissions to a @freezed class (keeping canMarkLiveCompletion as a computed getter rather than a constructor field, or a private default so it can't be set), and delete the hand-written ==/hashCode/copyWith.

title: Handle mid-loop failure in TutoredWriteRouter.pushStageDefinitions (tutored_write_router.dart)
rule: Nygard (partial I/O failure) / DB-6 offline-first parity
why: pushStageDefinitions awaits one Cloud Function call per stage sequentially and _handleResult throws immediately on the first TutorWriteFailure. If a tutor edits several stages at once and the network drops partway through, the earlier stages are already committed server-side while the remaining ones are simply lost — the thrown TutorWriteException names only the failing stage, not which stages already succeeded. Unlike the normal (non-tutored) write path, tutored writes deliberately bypass the local outbox (per this file's own header comment), so there is no retry queue to pick the dropped stages back up on reconnect — the class's offline-first guarantee (DB-6, exercised everywhere else in this app) does not hold here. This is architectural/edge-case reasoning, not a reproduced runtime failure.
recommendation: Either batch the per-stage calls into a single CF invocation (atomic on the server) or collect per-stage results and surface a structured partial-failure summary (which stages succeeded/failed) so the caller can retry just the failed subset instead of losing silent state.
acceptance_criteria: A test that fails the 2nd of 3 stage upserts asserts the caller learns which stages succeeded (not just a single opaque exception).
Documented decision (in tutored_write_router.dart's header) on whether partial multi-stage failure is an accepted risk or gets a retry path.

why: createTestDatabase() is a plain constructor call with no caching, so identical(db1, db2) is guaranteed false for any two invocations regardless of whether UserDatabase has any shared/static state that leaks data between instances — the assertion cannot fail even if isolation were genuinely broken. recommendation: Replace the identical() check with a real isolation assertion: insert a row into db1 (e.g. via seedProfile) and assert it is absent when querying db2, or that db2's relevant table starts empty. why: deploy-play-store.yml has no `needs:`/`workflow_run:` dependency on ci.yml and no step that checks the target SHA's check-run status. A maintainer who tags a commit that never went through review/CI (an emergency hotfix, a stale local branch, the wrong SHA) or whose ci.yml run is still red/in-progress can ship straight to Google Play production with nothing in the committed config to stop it — the only backstop is human diligence, which is exactly the kind of implicit, non-deterministic gate Rule 0 says not to rely on.
recommendation: Add a job that queries the GitHub Checks API for the deploying SHA's required workflows before the build/upload steps run (or trigger deploys via a `workflow_call` from a successful ci.yml run instead of independent `push: tags`/`workflow_dispatch` triggers).
acceptance_criteria: deploy-play-store.yml fails fast if the deploying SHA has no green ci.yml run, before any build/signing steps execute.
A dry run against a SHA with a failing/missing CI run demonstrates the new gate blocking the deploy.

title: Add a getIdToken(forceRefresh) primitive so a synced write hitting permission-denied/unauthenticated can recover

evidence.quote:
if (user == null) return null;
    await user.reload();

/// Delegates to the auth gateways in `lib/core/auth/`. Per layering rule 3,
/// this file MUST NOT import the firebase_auth SDK

why: AU-5 requires exactly one getIdToken(true) forced refresh plus a single retry when a synced write fails with permission-denied/unauthenticated. A repo-wide grep for 'getIdToken' returns zero hits in lib/. Neither FirebaseAuthGateway/FirebaseAuthGatewayImpl nor AuthRepository/AuthRepositoryImpl — the only classes layering Rule 3 permits to touch FirebaseAuth for this feature — expose any way to force-refresh the cached ID token; the closest method, reloadCurrentUser()/User.reload(), only refreshes profile fields (displayName, emailVerified), not the JWT/claims. A stale token (e.g. after a custom-claims change) therefore has no dedicated recovery path; a failing synced write can only retry against the same stale token via the outbox's generic exponential backoff until it dead-letters, and the only user-facing fix is a full sign-out/sign-in.
recommendation: Add Future<String?> getIdToken({bool forceRefresh = false}) to FirebaseAuthGateway/AuthRepository as a thin pass-through to User.getIdToken, and wire the outbox/push-pipeline's permission-denied handler to call it once with forceRefresh: true plus a single retry before falling through to the existing backoff.
acceptance_criteria: FirebaseAuthGateway/AuthRepository gain a getIdToken(forceRefresh: true) method with a unit test against the fake/mock gateway.
Outbox/push-pipeline regression test: inject permission-denied on first attempt, assert exactly one getIdToken(true) call plus one retry occurs before falling back to normal backoff.

title: Wire AuthStateNotifier to authStateChanges() instead of leaving a shadowed, unused stream-based authStateProvider
why: auth_providers.dart defines a genuinely stream-backed authStateProvider (Stream<AppUser?> authState(ref) => ref.watch(authRepositoryProvider).onAuthStateChanged()) — exactly the AU-4-compliant primitive. But the provider that actually drives session routing everywhere (AuthGuard, AppShell, this screen) is the differently-implemented, identically-named authStateProvider generated from AuthStateNotifier, which never watches or listens to that stream — forcing every screen needing both to hide/alias one of them (see the 'hide authStateProvider' import here and the 'as auth_state' alias in sign_in_controller.dart/signup_screen.dart). If Firebase invalidates a session server-side (disabled account, revoked refresh token, forced sign-out elsewhere) while the app is running, nothing re-derives AuthStateNotifier's state from that change — the app keeps believing the user is signed in until an unrelated explicit action happens to call reload/signOut. account_picker_screen.dart:274 shows the same non-reactive pattern at tile-badge granularity: hasValidSession is a one-shot ref.read(...).currentUser snapshot, not derived from the stream.
recommendation: Either delete the dead stream-based authState/authStateProvider if genuinely unused, or have AuthStateNotifier subscribe to it in build() so live Firebase-side session changes propagate into routing state, removing the need for every consumer to route around the name collision.

Regression test: emit a value on the mocked authStateChanges() stream after AuthStateNotifier has already resolved to signedIn, and assert the notifier's state updates without requiring an explicit signOut()/mutation call.

title: Fix LearningLedgerMerger's fallback ULID generator to avoid a permanent same-millisecond collision loss
rule: Nygard: silent, non-self-healing data loss on a manufactured natural-key collision
why: This fallback (only used when a pulled row has no `ulid` — 'legacy data' pre-migration docs, per the file's own comment) is deterministic with zero entropy: two ledger rows completed in the same millisecond with no ulid produce the IDENTICAL synthetic id. LearningLedgerDao dedups on ulid via INSERT OR IGNORE, so the second row is silently dropped — permanently, since a retry regenerates the same colliding id every time (unlike the rest of this merge layer's failures, which self-heal on the next pull because the underlying condition changes). A bulk-mark flow (bulk_mark_screen.dart is a named churn hotspot) writing several legacy-shaped completions together is a plausible trigger.
recommendation: Add entropy to the fallback id (e.g. an index-within-batch or random suffix instead of a constant zero-padded tail), or skip rows with no ulid and no way to disambiguate instead of manufacturing a collidable one.
acceptance_criteria: Unit test: merge two distinct legacy (no-ulid) rows sharing the same completed_at millisecond — assert both are inserted, not deduplicated into one.

corrections: The bulk_mark_screen.dart trigger example is unsupported: local ledger writes always assign a real ULID via newUlid(now) (learning_ledger_repository_impl.dart:107,174), so bulk-marking today cannot produce a no-ulid row. Only genuine pre-ULID-migration Firestore docs can reach the _makeUlid fallback; the core collision mechanism itself is confirmed correct.

title: Watch reactive auth state instead of ref.read-ing currentUser inside _AccountTileState.build()
why: SM-3 requires ref.watch in build and ref.read only in callbacks, precisely because a ref.read snapshot of a mutable getter (`.currentUser`, which changes on sign-in/out/re-auth without the authRepositoryProvider instance itself changing) is only re-evaluated when something else this widget DOES watch happens to force a rebuild — not when the underlying session actually changes. The tile's 'valid session' vs 'sign in again' pill/warning-icon can go stale after an auth event (e.g. a sibling tile's re-auth flow) that doesn't independently invalidate this tile.
recommendation: Replace with a watched, narrow selector, e.g. `ref.watch(authStateProvider.select((s) => s.currentUser?.firebaseUid))`, so the tile is reactive to session changes.
acceptance_criteria: A widget test changes the live Firebase session via a provider override while the picker is mounted and asserts the affected tile's badge updates without an unrelated rebuild trigger

title: Replace tautological ConstrainedBox-ancestor check in r2_panel_leaf_crumb_ellipsis_test.dart with a real width-bound assertion
why: Empirically verified via mutation testing: with the real fix in place, `flutter test` passes 4/4. Reverting hierarchy_selection_panel.dart's leaf-crumb Text to a bare `Text(label)` (no overflow/maxLines/ConstrainedBox) makes the suite RED as expected — but reverting only the `ConstrainedBox(maxWidth: maxLeafCrumbWidth)` wrapper while leaving `overflow: TextOverflow.ellipsis, maxLines: 1, softWrap: false` on the Text keeps all 4 cases GREEN. rule: Nygard lens — what happens when I/O fails halfway
why: Future.timeout() races a Timer against the lookup but cannot cancel the underlying OS-level DNS resolution — dart:io gives no cancellable primitive for InternetAddress.lookup. Under packet loss or a captive portal (exactly when this check matters most), the original lookup keeps running past the 2s timeout with no way to observe or cancel it; repeated calls (e.g. retrying a failed offline-account conversion in account_actions.dart) can accumulate abandoned lookups.
recommendation: Either document the accepted tradeoff inline (dart:io has no cancellable DNS API) with a bounded-impact justification, or switch to a primitive that supports cancellation (e.g. a raw socket connect with explicit close on timeout).
acceptance_criteria: Either an inline comment documents the accepted leak and its bound, or a test demonstrates no more than one lookup stays in flight after repeated rapid isOnline calls under a simulated timeout

corrections: account_actions.dart:226's isOnline call is inside showDeleteAccountFlow (delete-account-requires-internet), not an offline-account-conversion retry path; the core evidence at connectivity_gateway.dart:14 is unaffected.

title: Fail fast on missing key.properties instead of silently debug-signing release Android builds (build.gradle.kts)
rule: Tier-2 area note (security) — AG-11-adjacent CI guardrail soft-skip
why: When KEYSTORE_BASE64 is unset (misconfigured secret, or a maintainer manually dispatches the 'Build APK' workflow with build_type=release before secrets are wired up), build.yml prints a warning but does not fail — it proceeds to 'flutter build apk --release'. Because key.properties was never written, Gradle's fallback here silently signs the 'release' APK with the shared, publicly-known Flutter debug keystore, then uploads it as a GitHub Actions artifact literally named learning-tracker-release-apk. Anyone who installs that artifact believing it's a genuine release build gets a debug-signed binary; since the debug key is identical across virtually all Flutter/Android-Studio installs, another developer's debug-signed build could later 'update' over it without Android's signature check objecting.
recommendation: Make the release signingConfig fail fast (e.g. error("release build requested but key.properties is missing")) instead of silently substituting debug signing, or at minimum have build.yml's keystore-decode step exit 1 when build_type == 'release' and the secret is empty instead of only warning.
acceptance_criteria: flutter build apk --release (or ./gradlew assembleRelease) fails loudly when key.properties/keystore secret is absent, instead of producing a debug-signed 'release' artifact.
build.yml's release job aborts (non-zero exit) when KEYSTORE_BASE64 is empty and build_type=release.

corrections: docs/deployment-guide.md:25 documents the debug-signing fallback as intentional design ('falls back to debug signing if absent'), undercutting the 'silently' framing and the primary fail-hard-Gradle recommendation, which would break the documented local-dev flow. The 'debug key identical across installs' claim is also a common misconception: no shared debug.keystore is committed in this repo, and each machine/CI run auto-generates its own unique debug key, so there's no real cross-device signature-collision/update risk as described. The narrower, still-valid residual issue is that build.yml doesn't fail-fast when an explicit release dispatch is missing its secret, silently uploading a mislabeled artifact.

title: outboxSyncWriteFacadeProvider mutates DAO state and fires a network re-enqueue from inside its Provider build function

title: Type streak_milestone_analytics_observer.dart's two catch blocks to Exception — bare Object catches swallow Error subtypes as warnings
why: Neither catch has an `on X` clause, so both also catch Dart Error subtypes (NoSuchMethodError, TypeError, RangeError, StateError) that signal genuine programming bugs, not recoverable runtime conditions — exactly what EH-4 says never to catch. A bug in StreakStateProvider or an unexpected state shape gets downgraded to a single logger.warning(...) call (not even error/critical) and the loop or stream quietly continues or ends — no crash, no Crashlytics report, nothing but a line in a 2000-entry ring buffer nobody reviews outside 'Send Diagnostic Logs'. This provider runs unconditionally in the app shell every session (per its own doc comment), so a regression here has zero blast-radius signal to catch it.
recommendation: Narrow both catches to `on Exception catch (e, st)` (or the specific exception types StreakStateProvider/AnalyticsService can throw) and let Error subtypes propagate to the zone's onError handler like the rest of the app.
acceptance_criteria: Both catch clauses in streak_milestone_analytics_observer.dart use `on Exception catch` (or a named typed exception), not bare `catch (e, st)`
streak_milestone_analytics_observer_test.dart's existing R6-3 tests still pass unchanged (they throw plain Exception, not Error)

corrections: Ran a probe test: querying a closed Drift NativeDatabase throws StateError (e is Error==true, e is Exception==false) — the exact scenario R6-3's stream-error test triggers via db.close(). Narrowing line 83's catch to `on Exception` lets that StateError escape and flips state.hasError to true, breaking the existing green test the finding claims 'still pass unchanged.' Doc comment (lines 34-37) also documents the swallow-all behavior as deliberate, not accidental. Downgrading severity/confidence accordingly; the inner catch (line 74) is a cleaner, lower-stakes instance of the same rule violation.

title: core/time/local_day_clock.dart's currentLocalDayClock global has no compiler-enforced set/reset pairing for tests
rule: SM-7 spirit (no global/static mutable singletons) / TQ-6 hermetic tests
why: This mutable top-level variable backs DateTimeFactory, which is called from 15+ production sites across DAOs/repositories/mergers (e.g. track_dao.dart, a churn hotspot, calls it 8 times). A test file that calls useLocalDayClock() without the tearDown pairing would silently freeze time for every later test in that file/isolate, producing flaky failures unrelated to the code under test. I checked the two actual test files that use it (only outbox_processor_test.dart and one other) and both correctly pair set/reset via `tearDown(resetLocalDayClock)`, so this is a latent, convention-enforced risk rather than a demonstrated failure today.
recommendation: Add a shared test helper (e.g. `withFakeClock(seed, body)`) that calls `addTearDown(resetLocalDayClock)` itself so individual tests can't forget the reset, and migrate the existing 2 call sites to it.

title: Defensively copy SyncPushException.committed so the partial-commit invariant can't be violated by a future caller
rule: Evans lens — invariant enforced in one place, not by caller convention
why: SyncPushException.committed exists specifically so OutboxProcessor can tell which outbox rows genuinely landed before a batch failed, so committed rows are 'never re-pushed or dead-lettered' (per this file's own docstring, H3). That invariant currently holds only because the single production call site remembers to wrap the list in List.unmodifiable(pushed) before throwing — the exception class itself accepts any List<String>, including a live mutable reference, with no internal defensive copy. A future call site (or a test double standing in for one) that passes a growable list it keeps appending to after constructing the exception would silently corrupt the partial-commit accounting this type exists to protect, with no compiler or runtime signal that anything went wrong.
recommendation: Copy defensively inside the constructor (e.g. an initializer that wraps committed in List.unmodifiable(committed)) so the guarantee doesn't depend on every future caller remembering to do it themselves.
acceptance_criteria: a new unit test constructs SyncPushException with a growable list, mutates the original list after construction, and asserts .committed is unaffected

title: Remove or justify PushPipeline.pushCompletion — OutboxProcessor never calls it
why: OutboxProcessor's _dispatch switch has no case for OutboxEntityKind.completion — completions are handled exclusively via pushCompletionsBatch, consistent with the class doc's own warning ('Never call [pushCompletion] in a loop — that defeats the batching'). A repo-wide grep for `.pushCompletion(` shows the only caller of PushPipeline's (non-gateway) pushCompletion is test code calling it directly; production code never reaches it through the drain path. It's a fully implemented, individually tested, but currently unreachable interface method — dead surface area that invites drift (e.g. a future fix applied to pushCompletionsBatch but not mirrored here, or a future caller reintroducing the exact N-round-trip problem batching was built to eliminate).
recommendation: Either delete pushCompletion from PushPipeline (and its implementation/tests) or add a doc comment on the interface method naming its actual sanctioned caller/purpose so the next reader doesn't mistake it for reachable code.
acceptance_criteria: Grep confirms either the method is removed (and OutboxPushPipeline/tests updated) or a doc comment states its real caller.

title: Add a ref.mounted check after the await in resolveOwnerAccountIdForWipe (tutored_pull_providers.dart)
why: resolveOwnerAccountIdForWipe(Ref ref) awaits a DB query and then, on the fallback path, calls ref.read(currentAccountIdProvider) with no ref.mounted guard in between. Per SM-4/Riverpod 3, if the provider or notifier that owns this `ref` is disposed while the getAllUserProfiles() query is in flight (e.g. the reconcile fires during a sign-out or account switch that tears down the owning provider), this throws an uncaught UnmountedRefException from inside a bare async function with no surrounding try/catch at this call site.
recommendation: Add `if (!ref.mounted) return <safe fallback, e.g. -1 or rethrow a typed error>;` immediately after the awaited query, before the ref.read(currentAccountIdProvider) fallback.
acceptance_criteria: resolveOwnerAccountIdForWipe checks ref.mounted before any post-await ref access.
Regression test: dispose the owning container/provider during the awaited DB call and assert no UnmountedRefException escapes uncaught.

corrections: Severity lowered P2→P3: the function is dead code (test-only caller), so the described failure has zero current production cost — not a reachable/live SM-4 gap as framed. Should be resolved alongside whichever fix finding 4 lands (wire up or delete), not tracked as a standalone reachable risk.

title: Remove the dead no-op catchError in OutboxPushPipeline._runValue

title: Convert ReminderPreferences to @freezed instead of hand-rolled ==/hashCode/copyWith
why: Matches the coding standard's explicit rule to never hand-write ==/hashCode for data classes. The 7 fields are consistent between == and hashCode today, but every future field addition is a manual 3-way sync across the constructor, ==, hashCode and copyWith -- an easy place to introduce a silent equality bug (a field present in the constructor but missed in == makes two logically-different instances compare equal).
recommendation: Convert to @freezed class ReminderPreferences with _$ReminderPreferences.
acceptance_criteria: dart run build_runner build generates the freezed file and existing tests (e.g. notification_providers_deep_test.dart groups H/A-E) keep passing unmodified.

title: Fix the sefaria_ref_matcher_test.dart sortOrder test that cannot verify its own claim
rule: TQ-8 (assertion must match what the source can actually do wrong)

why: leafChildrenForContainer returns Set<String>, so any internal sort is erased before the caller sees it; the test's own comment admits this and falls back to containsAll (membership only, no order check), so the test cannot fail if the production sort() call were deleted entirely — its name promises an ordering guarantee the assertion never checks.
recommendation: Rename the test to describe what it actually checks (all three leaves present), or — if callers genuinely depend on order (resolveIndexedUnitRefs re-sorts independently, suggesting they don't) — change the return type to an ordered List and assert order for real.

title: Remove flutter_test_config.dart's FlutterError.onError GoogleFonts filter — TestWidgetsFlutterBinding never lets it run during a test
rule: Test-infra correctness (no direct coding-standards rule ID)
why: The comment above this block claims it suppresses 'residual font not found errors... cosmetic rendering issues, not test logic failures' during test execution. I traced the installed Flutter SDK (3.44.1, matching this repo's `flutter --version`): TestWidgetsFlutterBinding._runTest() (binding.dart:1770) saves whatever handler is currently installed into _oldExceptionHandler, then unconditionally overwrites FlutterError.onError with its own handler that just does `_pendingExceptionDetails = details` — it never calls the previously-installed handler. postTest() (binding.dart:2131-2134) restores _oldExceptionHandler only after the test body has finished. Since _runTest() wraps every individual test()/testWidgets() body, the custom GoogleFonts-substring filter installed in flutter_test_config.dart is captured as 'the old handler' before the first test and is never invoked while any test is actually running — exactly the window in which a font-not-found FlutterError would fire. If such an error does occur during a pump, it is captured into _pendingExceptionDetails and fails the test outright, contradicting the file's own comment about what it does.
recommendation: Delete the dead FlutterError.onError override (lines 17-22), or replace it with a mechanism proven to run mid-test (e.g. wrap only the specific pump inside affected tests, or fix the font-loading gap in finding 'golden_runner.dart never renders real glyphs' so the underlying error stops occurring). Do not rely on a global onError swap in this file for anything that needs to suppress errors during pumpWidget/pumpAndSettle.
acceptance_criteria: A widget test that deliberately throws/renders a FlutterError whose message contains 'GoogleFonts' mid-pump either fails (proving the current filter does nothing) or is demonstrated to pass only via a mechanism that actually executes during _runTest's window.
The doc comment above the handler is removed or corrected to match what the code can actually do.

title: Replace ws3_3e_dual_role_fix_test.dart's naive method-body string slice with depth-matched brace extraction
why: The helper extracts a Dart method's body by finding the FIRST line that is exactly two spaces + '}' after the method start, instead of counting brace depth. It happens to work today only because _isTutorSession is a one-line method; the same fragile logic is duplicated a second time in the same file (AC2, ~line 72-75) instead of being factored out. The codebase already has the correct depth-counting version right next door — _extractRuleBlock in w3_41_tutor_security_rules_test.dart:438-459 — that this file doesn't reuse. If _isTutorSession ever grows a nested block whose closing brace lands at the same 2-space indent, the slice truncates early and the isNot(contains(...)) assertion would pass regardless of what the unseen remainder of the method does.
recommendation: Extract _extractRuleBlock-style depth-counting into a shared test helper and use it for method-body extraction here instead of the raw indexOf heuristic; de-duplicate the two inline copies in this file.
acceptance_criteria: ws3_3e_dual_role_fix_test.dart's method-body extraction uses depth-matched brace counting (or a shared helper), with a regression case where the target method contains a nested block closing at the same indent.

corrections: Duplication (lines 53/74), _isTutorSession's 1-line body, and the unused _extractRuleBlock depth-counter (w3_41 file:438-459) are all verified real. But the stated trigger ('nested block lands at same 2-space indent') is inaccurate: dart format indents nested blocks to 4+ spaces inside a 2-space method, so they can't collide with '\n  }'. A doc-comment or raw-string literal containing an embedded 2-space '}' is the realistic trigger instead. Core duplication/fragility defect still holds regardless.

title: Narrow the swallow-all catch in gamification_p1_test.dart's _loadMilestones test helper
why: _loadMilestones backs the final assertion of 4 tests (E2E-605/606/607/613) that all compare SharedPreferences-persisted reward milestones against expected titles. A bare `catch (_) { return const []; }` around the JSON decode+map turns ANY exception — a genuine RewardMilestone.fromJson schema-mismatch bug, JSON corruption, a typo in the config key — into a silently-returned empty list. A real production regression here would surface only as a confusing 'expected isNotEmpty, got []' failure, with the actual exception and stack trace discarded, instead of pointing at the real defect.
recommendation: Let the exception propagate (test helpers should fail loudly), or catch only the specific expected type (e.g. FormatException from jsonDecode) and rethrow anything else.
acceptance_criteria: _loadMilestones no longer has a bare `catch (_)`; either no catch, or a narrowly-typed catch that rethrows for unexpected exceptions

title: Tighten v16_to_v17_test.dart's FK-violation assertion beyond throwsA(anything)
why: The test's stated purpose is "C2: FK enforcement must reject completion with non-existent profileId", but `throwsA(anything)` is satisfied by ANY thrown object — a coincidental exception from unrelated test-setup breakage would make this pass without the FK constraint under test ever being exercised, silently losing the regression coverage it claims to provide. Every later migration-gate test in this same directory that checks a similar constraint (v25_to_v27_test.dart, v27_to_v28_test.dart) uses a typed matcher (`isA<SqliteException>()`/`isA<Exception>()`), so this is a real regression in assertion discipline, not a stylistic choice.
recommendation: Narrow to `throwsA(isA<SqliteException>())` (or the concrete exception type Drift/sqlite3 raises for an FK violation), matching the pattern used elsewhere in this same test directory.
acceptance_criteria: v16_to_v17_test.dart's FK test asserts a specific exception type, not `anything`

title: Decode xz's stderr before interpolating it in seed_content_db.dart's failure message (currently prints a raw byte list)
why: Process.runSync is called at line 312-317 with `stderrEncoding: null`, so ProcessResult.stderr holds raw bytes (a Uint8List), not a decoded String. String-interpolating it at line 319 invokes List.toString(), producing something like 'xz failed: [120, 122, 58, 32, ...]' instead of xz's actual human-readable stderr text — exactly when a maintainer most needs a readable error, during a failing release build.
recommendation: Pass `stderrEncoding: systemEncoding` (or explicit `utf8`) to this Process.runSync call, or explicitly `utf8.decode(xzResult.stderr as List<int>)` before interpolating it into the thrown StateError.
acceptance_criteria: Triggering an xz failure (e.g. temporarily pointing dbPath at a nonexistent file, or aliasing xz unavailable) prints a human-readable message, not a numeric byte-list
seed_content_db.dart's xz Process.runSync call sets stderrEncoding to a real Encoding, or decodes stderr before use

title: Pin distributionSha256Sum in android/gradle/wrapper/gradle-wrapper.properties
why: The wrapper properties file has no distributionSha256Sum key. Without it, gradlew's bootstrap download of the Gradle distribution has no integrity check beyond TLS — a compromised mirror/CDN or a MITM on a misconfigured proxy could substitute a malicious Gradle distribution that every subsequent local build and CI run would silently execute.
recommendation: Run `./gradlew wrapper --gradle-version 8.14 --distribution-type all` (or add distributionSha256Sum manually from Gradle's published checksums page) so the wrapper verifies the download and fails closed on mismatch.
acceptance_criteria: gradle-wrapper.properties contains a distributionSha256Sum line matching the official checksum for gradle-8.14-all.zip.
A deliberately-wrong checksum causes ./gradlew to fail the download instead of proceeding.
